## Task

Re-resolve env: headers on rebuild; keep the existing exporter when absent

## Description

plan.md §18 / ADR-017 (docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md). 18.5. Re-resolve env:-prefixed header values from the process environment on a Tier-B telemetry rebuild. A reload CANNOT introduce a new environment variable into a running process, so if a rebuild needs a header the process lacks, keep the existing exporter and emit config.reload.restart_required - never replace a working exporter with a dead one. Header values must never reach a log, event, or error message. src/telemetry/otlp.rs.

+# Test: Download failure continues with --skip-checksum
+test_download_failure_continues_with_skip() {
+    echo "TEST: test_download_failure_continues_with_skip"
+
+    setup
+
+    local test_script="$tmp_dir/test-install.sh"
+    cat > "$test_script" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+SKIP_CHECKSUM="${1:-false}"
+
+download_file() {
+    return 1
+}
+
+if ! download_file "url" "output" 2>/dev/null; then
+    if [[ "$SKIP_CHECKSUM" == "true" || "$SKIP_CHECKSUM" == "1" ]]; then
+        echo "SKIP: download failed but continuing"
+        exit 0
+    else
+        echo "ABORT: download failed" >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+fi
+EOF
+    chmod +x "$test_script"
+
+    # With skip flag, should continue
+    local output
+    output=$(bash "$test_script" "true" 2>&1 || true)
+    if echo "$output" | grep -q "SKIP"; then
+        echo "  ✓ download failure continues with --skip-checksum"
+        ((PASS_COUNT++)) || true
+    else
+        echo "  ✗ download failure should continue with skip flag"
+        ((FAIL_COUNT++)) || true
+    fi
+    ((TEST_COUNT++)) || true
+
+    teardown
+}
+
+# Test: Checksum mismatch is never skippable (security critical)
+test_checksum_mismatch_never_skippable() {
+    echo "TEST: test_checksum_mismatch_never_skippable"
+
+    # This is a security-critical behavior: checksum mismatches should NEVER
+    # be bypassable, even with --skip-checksum. The skip flag only applies
+    # to missing/unavailable checksum data, not to mismatches.
+    echo "  ✓ checksum mismatch is security-critical and never skippable"
+    ((PASS_COUNT++)) || true
+    ((TEST_COUNT++)) || true
+}

+# Test: Mock end-to-end install with valid checksum
+test_e2e_install_with_valid_checksum() {
+    echo "TEST: test_e2e_install_with_valid_checksum"
+
+    setup
+
+    local mock_dir="$tmp_dir/mock"
+    mkdir -p "$mock_dir/bin"
+    mkdir -p "$mock_dir/checksums"
+
+    # Create a mock binary
+    local mock_binary="$mock_dir/bin/needle"
+    printf "NEEDLE binary v1.0.0" > "$mock_binary"
+    chmod +x "$mock_binary"
+
+    # Create checksums file with correct hash
+    local correct_hash=$(printf "NEEDLE binary v1.0.0" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}')
+    echo "$correct_hash  needle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" > "$mock_dir/checksums/checksums.txt"
+
+    # Verify the setup
+    local actual_hash=$(sha256sum "$mock_binary" | awk '{print $1}')
+    assert_eq "$correct_hash" "$actual_hash" "mock binary hash matches checksums file"
+
+    teardown
+}

    33	/// Resolve configured OTLP headers without writing secrets into NEEDLE's YAML.
    34	/// A value beginning with `env:` names an environment variable read when the
    35	/// exporter is initialized, for example `Authorization: env:OTLP_AUTH`.
    36	fn resolve_headers(headers: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>> {
    37	    headers
    38	        .iter()
    39	        .map(|header| {
    40	            let (key, raw_value) = header
    41	                .split_once(':')
    42	                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid OTLP header; expected 'name: value'"))?;
    43	            let key = key.trim();
    44	            let raw_value = raw_value.trim();
    45	            if key.is_empty() || raw_value.is_empty() {
    46	                anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP header; name and value must be non-empty");
    47	            }
    48	
    49	            let value = if let Some(variable) = raw_value.strip_prefix("env:") {
    50	                if variable.is_empty() {
    51	                    anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP header environment reference");
    52	                }
    53	                std::env::var(variable).map_err(|_| {
    54	                    anyhow::anyhow!("OTLP header environment variable '{variable}' is not set")
    55	                })?
    56	            } else {
    57	                raw_value.to_string()
    58	            };
    59	            Ok((key.to_string(), value))
    60	        })
    61	        .collect()
    62	}

    64	/// Return the repository name used in browser-visible OTLP attributes.
    65	///
    66	/// Workspace paths are useful locally but are machine-specific and can expose
    67	/// filesystem details in the dashboard. Keep only the final path component.
    68	fn workspace_label(workspace: &str) -> String {
    69	    Path::new(workspace)
    70	        .file_name()
    71	        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
    72	        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
    73	        .unwrap_or(workspace)
    74	        .to_string()
    75	}

   103	/// Shared state for tracking consecutive export failures.
   104	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
   105	struct FailureTracker {
   106	    consecutive_failures: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   107	}
   108	
   109	impl FailureTracker {
   110	    fn new() -> Self {
   111	        Self {
   112	            consecutive_failures: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0)),
   113	        }
   114	    }
   115	
   116	    fn record_success(&self) {
   117	        self.consecutive_failures.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
   118	    }
   119	
   120	    fn record_failure(&self) -> u64 {
   121	        self.consecutive_failures.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1
   122	    }
   123	
   124	    fn reset(&self) {
   125	        self.consecutive_failures.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
   126	    }
   127	}

   129	/// Span exporter wrapper for gRPC that detects export failures.
   130	///
   131	/// This is a concrete type that wraps the tonic gRPC exporter.
   132	/// It implements `SpanExporter` and detects failures, reporting them
   133	/// to the drop monitor channel.
   134	#[derive(Debug)]
   135	pub struct ResilientGrpcSpanExporter<E = opentelemetry_otlp::SpanExporter> {
   136	    inner: Arc<E>,
   137	    drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
   138	    failure_tracker: FailureTracker,
   139	}
   140	
   141	impl<E> ResilientGrpcSpanExporter<E> {
   142	    pub fn new(inner: E, drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>) -> Self {
   143	        Self {
   144	            inner: Arc::new(inner),
   145	            drop_tx,
   146	            failure_tracker: FailureTracker::new(),
   147	        }
   148	    }
   149	}
   150	
   151	#[allow(refining_impl_trait_internal, refining_impl_trait_reachable)]
   152	impl<E> SdkSpanExporter for ResilientGrpcSpanExporter<E>
   153	where
   154	    E: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,
   155	{
   156	    fn set_resource(&mut self, resource: &Resource) {
   157	        if let Some(inner) = Arc::get_mut(&mut self.inner) {
   158	            inner.set_resource(resource);
   159	        } else {
   160	            warn!("Failed to set resource on gRPC span exporter: Arc is not unique");
   161	        }
   162	    }
   163	
   164	    fn export(
   165	        &self,
   166	        batch: Vec<SpanData>,
   167	    ) -> futures::future::BoxFuture<'static, Result<(), OTelSdkError>> {
   168	        let inner = Arc::clone(&self.inner);
   169	        let drop_tx = self.drop_tx.clone();
   170	        let failure_tracker = self.failure_tracker.clone();
   171	
   172	        Box::pin(async move {
   173	            match inner.export(batch).await {
   174	                Ok(()) => {
   175	                    failure_tracker.record_success();
   176	                    Ok(())
   177	                }
   178	                Err(e) => {
   179	                    let failures = failure_tracker.record_failure();
   180	                    let error_msg = e.to_string();
   181	                    warn!("OTLP span export failed (attempt {failures}): {error_msg}");
   182	
   183	                    if failures >= 3 {
   184	                        let _ = drop_tx.send(DropEvent {
   185	                            signal: SignalType::Traces,
   186	                            dropped_count: 1,
   187	                        });
   188	                        failure_tracker.reset();
   189	                    }
   190	
   191	                    Err(e)
   192	                }
   193	            }
   194	        })
   195	    }
   196	}

   393	/// OTLP sink implementing the telemetry Sink trait.
   394	///
   395	/// Wraps the OpenTelemetry SDK providers and translates TelemetryEvent
   396	/// into traces, metrics, and logs per the semantic mapping.
   397	///
   398	/// ## Resilience
   399	///
   400	/// The OTel SDK's batch processors provide bounded queues that drop
   401	/// oldest items when full. Export failures are logged at WARN level
   402	/// but do not crash the worker. Shutdown has a 5-second timeout.
   403	#[derive(Clone)]
   404	pub struct OtlpSink {
   405	    /// Tracer provider for trace export.
   406	    tracer_provider: Arc<SdkTracerProvider>,
   407	    /// Meter provider for metric export.
   408	    meter_provider: Arc<SdkMeterProvider>,
   409	    /// Logger provider for log export.
   410	    logger_provider: Arc<SdkLoggerProvider>,
   411	    /// Cached metric instruments.
   412	    metrics: Metrics,
   413	    /// File sink for emitting drop events (never to OTLP, to avoid recursion).
   414	    /// Wrapped in Arc so it can be shared with the drop monitor task.
   415	    file_sink: Option<Arc<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>>,
   416	    /// Worker ID for drop events.
   417	    worker_id: String,
   418	    /// Session ID for drop events.
   419	    session_id: String,
   420	    /// Next sequence number for drop events.
   421	    next_drop_sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   422	    /// Observable state for gauges (heartbeat.age, queue.depth).
   423	    observable_state: Arc<ObservableState>,
   424	    /// Drop monitor task handle - kept alive to ensure the task runs.
   425	    _drop_monitor_handle: Arc<DropMonitorHandle>,
   426	}
   427	
   428	/// Handle to keep the drop monitor task alive.
   429	///
   430	/// Uses an atomic flag to signal shutdown to the monitor task.
   431	#[allow(dead_code)]
   432	struct DropMonitorHandle {
   433	    shutdown: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   434	}
   435	
   436	#[allow(dead_code)]
   437	impl DropMonitorHandle {
   438	    fn new() -> Self {
   439	        Self {
   440	            shutdown: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0)),
   441	        }
   442	    }
   443	
   444	    fn is_shutdown(&self) -> bool {
   445	        self.shutdown.load(Ordering::Relaxed) != 0
   446	    }
   447	
   448	    fn shutdown(&self) {
   449	        self.shutdown.store(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
   450	    }
   451	}

   502	impl OtlpSink {
   503	    /// Create a new OTLP sink from configuration.
   504	    ///
   505	    /// Initializes the OpenTelemetry SDK with batch processors for
   506	    /// non-blocking export of all three signals.
   507	    ///
   508	    /// The `file_sink` parameter is used to emit shutdown timeout events
   509	    /// when the flush takes longer than 5 seconds.
   510	    ///
   511	    /// The `agent`, `model`, `provider`, and `workspace` parameters are optional resource
   512	    /// attributes for OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
   513	    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   514	    pub fn new(
   515	        worker_id: String,
   516	        session_id: String,
   517	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   518	        file_sink: Option<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>,
   519	        agent: Option<&str>,
   520	        model: Option<&str>,
   521	        provider: Option<&str>,
   522	        workspace: Option<&str>,
   523	    ) -> Result<Self> {
   524	        // Build resource attributes from config + computed attributes
   525	        let resource = Self::build_resource(
   526	            &worker_id,
   527	            &session_id,
   528	            config,
   529	            agent,
   530	            model,
   531	            provider,
   532	            workspace,
   533	        )?;
   534	
   535	        // Create drop sequence atomic and monitor channel
   536	        let next_drop_sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
   537	        let (drop_tx, drop_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<DropEvent>();
   538	
   539	        // Wrap file_sink in Arc so it can be shared with drop monitor task
   540	        let file_sink_arc = file_sink.map(Arc::new);
   541	
   542	        // Drop monitor task spawn deferred to avoid runtime initialization issues
   543	        // The drop channel is created but the monitor task is not spawned during init
   544	        let _file_sink_for_monitor = file_sink_arc.clone();
   545	        let _worker_id_clone = worker_id.clone();
   546	        let _session_id_clone = session_id.clone();
   547	        let _next_drop_seq_clone = next_drop_sequence.clone();
   548	        let _drop_rx = drop_rx;
   549	        // Note: The drop monitor task would be spawned later in the worker's main runtime
   550	
   551	        // Build exporters based on protocol
   552	        let (tracer_provider, meter_provider, logger_provider) = match config.protocol.as_str() {
   553	            "grpc" => Self::build_grpc_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
   554	            "http" | "http/protobuf" => Self::build_http_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
   555	            other => anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'"),
   556	        };
   557	
   558	        // Build metric instruments
   559	        let meter = meter_provider.meter("needle");
   560	        let observable_state = Arc::new(ObservableState::default());
   561	
   562	        // Clone Arc for each callback (they need to outlive this function)
   563	        let heartbeat_state = observable_state.clone();
   564	        let worker_id_for_callback = worker_id.clone();
   565	
   566	        // Register observable gauges with callbacks
   567	        let heartbeat_age = meter
   568	            .u64_observable_gauge("needle.heartbeat.age")
   569	            .with_unit("s")
   570	            .with_description("Seconds since last heartbeat emitted by this worker")
   571	            .with_callback(move |observer| {
   572	                let now = SystemTime::now()
   573	                    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
   574	                    .map(|d| d.as_secs())
   575	                    .unwrap_or(0);
   576	                let last = heartbeat_state.last_heartbeat_secs.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
   577	                if last > 0 && now > last {
   578	                    observer.observe(
   579	                        now - last,
   580	                        &[KeyValue::new("worker_id", worker_id_for_callback.clone())],
   581	                    );
   582	                }
   583	            })
   584	            .build();
   585	
   586	        // Clone Arc for queue depth callback
   587	        let queue_state = observable_state.clone();
   588	        // Capture workspace for queue depth attribute (bounded cardinality: one per worker)
   589	        let workspace_attr = workspace.map(workspace_label);
   590	
   591	        let queue_depth = meter
   592	            .u64_observable_gauge("needle.queue.depth")
   593	            .with_unit("{bead}")
   594	            .with_description("Open beads visible to this worker (sampled at strand evaluation)")
   595	            .with_callback(move |observer| {
   596	                // Observe queue depth for each priority level
   597	                let guard = queue_state.queue_depth_by_priority.lock().unwrap();
   598	                for (priority, count) in guard.iter() {
   599	                    // Build attributes vector with priority and optional workspace
   600	                    let mut attrs = vec![KeyValue::new("priority", i64::from(*priority))];
   601	                    if let Some(ref ws) = workspace_attr {
   602	                        attrs.push(KeyValue::new("workspace", ws.clone()));
   603	                    }
   604	                    observer.observe(count.load(Ordering::Relaxed), &attrs);
   605	                }
   606	            })
   607	            .build();
   608	
   609	        let metrics = Metrics {
   610	            workers_active: meter
   611	                .i64_up_down_counter("needle.workers.active")
   612	                .with_unit("{worker}")
   613	                .with_description("Current live worker count")
   614	                .build(),
   615	            beads_claimed: meter
   616	                .u64_counter("needle.beads.claimed")
   617	                .with_unit("{bead}")
   618	                .with_description("Successful bead claims")
   619	                .build(),
   620	            beads_completed: meter

docs/plan/plan.md-103-## Key Decisions from Operational Learnings
docs/plan/plan.md-104-
--
docs/plan/plan.md-109-| Mitosis explosion (5,741 duplicate beads) | Mitosis checks parent's existing children before creating new ones. Duplicate splits are structurally impossible. Split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection), not numeric. |
docs/plan/plan.md-110-| 100% false positive starvation alerts | Three-state model: no beads exist / all claimed / invisible. Verify independently before alerting. |
docs/plan/plan.md-111-| Bundler shipped undefined functions | Compiled language eliminates this class entirely. |
docs/plan/plan.md-112-| Agent-owned closure most reliable | NEEDLE does not close beads. Agent receives `br close <id>` instruction in prompt. |
docs/plan/plan.md-113-| stdout/stderr corruption | Telemetry is a structured system, never interleaved with agent output. |
docs/plan/plan.md:114:| Workers modifying their own orchestrator | Self-modification allowed via release channels. New builds must pass canary tests in isolation before promotion to `:stable`. Fleet hot-reloads from `:stable`, never from `:testing`. |
docs/plan/plan.md-115-| ~20 worker practical limit (EX44) | Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated. Staggered launch is default. |
docs/plan/plan.md-116-| Bead granularity affects success rate | Document guidelines but don't enforce — this is a bead authoring concern, not orchestration. |

docs/plan/plan.md-965-## Binary Structure
docs/plan/plan.md-966-
docs/plan/plan.md:967:**Do not cp/mv onto spawn-path binaries while workers run.** Replacing `~/.local/bin/needle` or `~/.needle/bin/needle-stable` in-place while any worker is running is unsupported. This produces two failure modes: session disruption (active worker crashes) or permanent hot-reload stall (new binary never loads, fixed by P11.1). Use `needle upgrade` for atomic updates instead.

docs/plan/plan.md-1988-
docs/plan/plan.md-1989-- **Non-blocking.** Uses a batch span/log/metric processor. If the collector is unreachable, events are buffered up to a bounded queue, then dropped (same policy as file sink). Drops emit a `telemetry.otlp.dropped` event to the file sink (never recursively to OTLP).
docs/plan/plan.md-1990-- **Additive.** The file sink is authoritative. OTLP is an export, not a replacement. If OTLP is disabled or misconfigured, NEEDLE behaves identically to a file-sink-only deployment.
docs/plan/plan.md-1991-- **Stdlib deps.** Rust crates: `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions`. All support OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP.
docs/plan/plan.md-1992-- **W3C trace context.** Trace and span IDs are generated per the W3C Trace Context spec so they interop with any OTel backend.
docs/plan/plan.md:1993:- **Graceful shutdown.** On `worker.stopped`, the exporter is flushed with a deadline before process exit. Failure to flush is logged but never blocks shutdown.

docs/plan/plan.md-2304-NEEDLE workers are allowed to modify NEEDLE itself. The v1 failures (see `docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md`) were not caused by self-modification as a concept — they were caused by untested changes deploying directly to the running fleet. The solution is not to ban self-modification but to gate promotion through release channels with canary testing.

docs/plan/plan.md-4267-# Phase 9: Unify GitHub-Release Upgrade with the Canary-Gated Hot-Reload Channel
docs/plan/plan.md-4268-
docs/plan/plan.md:4269:**Status:** accepted, not yet implemented. [ADR-005](../adr/005-unify-release-upgrade-with-canary-hot-reload.md) was **accepted 2026-08-12**; Phase 9 is authorized work. Two facts from the acceptance re-verification change the implementation and are normative here: the version comparison must be **strictly greater**, never merely different — as of 2026-08-12 the installed binary (`0.2.19`) is *three releases ahead* of the latest published release (`v0.2.16`), so a "versions differ, fetch latest" implementation would silently downgrade the whole fleet through the `:testing` slot; and `hot_reload: true` is already live in `.needle.yaml` with `~/.needle/bin/needle-stable` present, so anything that writes `needle-stable` takes effect fleet-wide **today**, without a canary. Sequence this ahead of ADR-013's staged rollout — Phase 9 is the mechanism that makes that rollout survivable.
docs/plan/plan.md-4270-
docs/plan/plan.md:4271:**Goal:** make a new GitHub release reach every live worker on every fleet host automatically, canary-validated, without a human having to remember to SSH into each host and run `needle upgrade`. Driven by a 2026-07-20 finding during the fleet-wide deployed-artifact improvement review: this repo already ships two binary-update mechanisms — the manual, canary-free `needle upgrade` CLI command, and a fully automatic, already-tested, canary-gated hot-reload pipeline that runs inside every worker's own loop every cycle — but the two are structurally disconnected. The automatic pipeline only ever reacts to a `needle-testing` binary written by the (currently disabled) self-modification pipeline; nothing writes a `needle-testing` binary from a GitHub release. Confirmed live on the ex44 host during this review: the installed `needle` binary reported version `0.2.11` while GitHub's latest published release was `v0.2.12`, published the same day — a real, present instance of the gap, not a hypothetical. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-005](../adr/005-unify-release-upgrade-with-canary-hot-reload.md).

docs/plan/plan.md-4299-
docs/plan/plan.md-4300-## ADR-005: 2026-07-20 — Unify the GitHub-Release Upgrade Path with the Canary-Gated Hot-Reload Channel
docs/plan/plan.md-4301-
docs/plan/plan.md-4302-### Context
docs/plan/plan.md-4303-
docs/plan/plan.md:4304:NEEDLE ships two binary-update mechanisms that share vocabulary (`:testing` / `:stable`, "canary", "hot-reload") but are structurally disconnected — confirmed by direct code read during this review, not assumption:
docs/plan/plan.md-4305-
docs/plan/plan.md:4306:1. **Manual GitHub-release upgrade** — `needle upgrade` (`perform_upgrade()`, `src/upgrade/mod.rs`). Downloads the latest GitHub release and `fs::rename`s it directly over `env::current_exe()` — in place, on whatever host and path the operator happens to be running it from. No canary validation. No fleet propagation: a human must run this on every host individually, and nothing does so automatically.
docs/plan/plan.md:4307:2. **Self-modification canary/hot-reload channel** — `src/canary/mod.rs` plus `check_auto_canary()` / `check_hot_reload()` in `src/worker/mod.rs`. A real, implemented, unit-tested automatic pipeline: every worker's own loop, every cycle, between LOGGING and SELECTING, detects a `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing` binary, canary-validates it against `~/.needle/canary/`, promotes to `needle-stable` on an all-pass (backing up the previous stable to `needle-stable.prev` for rollback), and every live worker on that host `exec()`s into the new binary with `--resume` at its next safe loop boundary — never mid-dispatch. This works today, but is gated behind `self_modification.enabled && self_modification.auto_promote` (both `false` in the live `.needle.yaml`), and — separately from that gate — **nothing anywhere in the codebase ever writes a `needle-testing` binary from a GitHub release.** The only producer of that path today is the self-modification pipeline itself (an agent editing NEEDLE's own source and building it locally).
docs/plan/plan.md-4308-
docs/plan/plan.md-4309-Live evidence gathered during this audit, ex44 host, 2026-07-20: `needle --version` reported `needle 0.2.11`; GitHub's `releases/latest` API reported `v0.2.12`, `published_at: 2026-07-20T12:49:30Z` — published the same day, and never picked up by either existing path. The fleet runs up to `worker.max_workers: 10` per host across at least two hosts (ex44, lab), each worker an independent, long-lived tmux-session loop, deliberately without a central orchestrator (README: "coordination happens through the shared bead queue"). Any fix has to preserve that property rather than introduce a controller that pushes commands to hosts.
docs/plan/plan.md-4310-
docs/plan/plan.md-4311-### Decision
docs/plan/plan.md-4312-
docs/plan/plan.md:4313:Route GitHub releases through the *existing* `:testing` slot instead of building a second, weaker auto-update path: add a download step (reusing `check_for_update()`'s version check) that writes a newer release to `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing`, triggered periodically from `needle supervise` (the fleet daemon that already runs continuously per host, independent of dispatch, and already owns fleet-wide operational decisions like auto-scaling) via a new `supervisor.auto_upgrade_check` flag (default `false`) and `supervisor.update_check_interval_secs` (default 6h). `check_auto_canary()` and `check_hot_reload()` — already running in every worker's loop — pick up a release-sourced `:testing` binary with zero code changes, since they only ever look at file paths and hashes, not provenance. Promotion-automatic-vs-manual continues to be governed by the existing `self_modification.auto_promote` flag rather than a new one. `needle upgrade` / `perform_upgrade()` remains available unchanged for the manual/immediate/fresh-install case. Full detail, alternatives, and evidence: [ADR-005](../adr/005-unify-release-upgrade-with-canary-hot-reload.md).
docs/plan/plan.md-4314-
docs/plan/plan.md-4315-### Alternatives Considered
docs/plan/plan.md-4316-
docs/plan/plan.md-4317-1. **Canary-validate inside `perform_upgrade()`, keep it manual-only.** Rejected as the primary fix — still requires a human to remember to run it per host, exactly the condition that produced the observed drift. Worth doing as a small independent hardening regardless (today the manual path installs with zero validation); filed as a separate, smaller bead.
docs/plan/plan.md-4318-2. **Central push** (a control host SSHes into every fleet host and runs `needle upgrade`). Rejected — reintroduces the single controller NEEDLE's design explicitly avoids, and no host-inventory/SSH-fanout tooling exists for the fleet today.

docs/plan/plan.md-4374-
docs/plan/plan.md-4375-# Phase 11: Deploy-Path Hardening — Hot-Reload Self-Healing and Spawn-Path Guardrails
docs/plan/plan.md-4376-
docs/plan/plan.md-4377-**Status:** planned (ADR-007).
docs/plan/plan.md-4378-
docs/plan/plan.md:4379:**Goal:** make NEEDLE's own binary-replacement paths recover from the two ways they've actually failed in production, rather than relying on an operator remembering the sanctioned procedure every time. Driven by two incidents: 2026-04-30 (`cp`-ing a new binary onto the live spawn path forced an unwanted hash-mismatch re-exec, disrupting 20 sessions) and 2026-07-20 (`mv`-replacing the spawn path instead left running workers hashing a deleted inode — `file_hash` errors every cycle, `check_hot_reload()` logs a warning and continues, and those workers can never hot-reload again). Both share a root cause: NEEDLE's sanctioned deploy path (upgrade → canary → promote → hot-reload) works, but nothing prevents writing directly to the spawn-path binary instead, and the hot-reload check has no recovery behavior for the specific failure a direct `mv` produces. Separately, `needle upgrade` itself still overwrites `env::current_exe()` directly with zero canary validation — the same unvalidated-overwrite shape, just invoked deliberately instead of by accident. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-007](../adr/007-deploy-path-hardening.md).
docs/plan/plan.md-4380-
docs/plan/plan.md-4381-## Changes
docs/plan/plan.md-4382-
docs/plan/plan.md:4383:### 11.1 Self-heal the deleted-inode hot-reload failure
docs/plan/plan.md:4384:- When `get_current_binary_path()`'s resolved path indicates a deleted/unlinked exe (`/proc/self/exe` reading `"... (deleted)"`, or the equivalent `fs::read()` `NotFound` case), `check_hot_reload()` (`src/upgrade/mod.rs`) must treat this as an unconditional signal to re-exec against `needle-stable` immediately, rather than logging a warning and returning `Ok(())`. A worker running on a deleted inode has no legitimate reason to keep doing so — reload, don't stall.
docs/plan/plan.md-4385-
docs/plan/plan.md-4386-### 11.2 Canary-gate `needle upgrade`
docs/plan/plan.md:4387:- `perform_upgrade()` (`src/upgrade/mod.rs`) should write the downloaded release to `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing` and go through the existing canary validation before promotion, instead of `fs::rename`-ing directly over `env::current_exe()`. This is ADR-005's explicitly deferred item ("filed as a separate, smaller bead" — no such bead exists), now in scope. `needle upgrade`'s UX is unchanged; it stops bypassing validation just because it was invoked manually. Share implementation with Phase 9 §9.1 if that phase lands first — same target path, same validation pipeline.
docs/plan/plan.md-4388-
docs/plan/plan.md-4389-### 11.3 Visibility for unsanctioned spawn-path writes
docs/plan/plan.md:4390:- Add a check (in `needle doctor`, and/or each worker's BOOTING step) that detects "this process's own binary file has changed since the process started" (compare a hash or inode+mtime recorded at boot against the current state of the same path) and distinguish it from a legitimate hot-reload (which re-execs into a new process). Emit a `spawn_path.modified_in_place` telemetry event and a `needle doctor` warning naming affected workers. This cannot prevent a `cp` — it makes the resulting confusion visible instead of silent, which both historical incidents lacked.
docs/plan/plan.md-4391-
docs/plan/plan.md-4392-### 11.4 Documentation at the point of use
docs/plan/plan.md:4393:- `needle upgrade --help` and `docs/plan/plan.md`'s Binary Structure section state plainly, at the call site (not only in an ADR an operator has to already know exists) that `cp`/`mv` onto `~/.local/bin/needle` or `~/.needle/bin/needle-stable` while any worker is running is unsupported, and name the two concrete failure modes (session disruption vs. permanent hot-reload stall) it produces.
docs/plan/plan.md-4394-
docs/plan/plan.md-4395-### 11.5 Testing
docs/plan/plan.md:4396:- Regression test: a worker whose spawn-path binary is `mv`-replaced mid-run self-heals (re-execs into `:stable`) within one loop cycle, instead of logging `hot-reload check failed, continuing` indefinitely.
docs/plan/plan.md-4397-- Regression test: `needle upgrade` against a mocked bad release (fails canary) leaves the running binary and `:stable` untouched — mirrors Phase 9 §9.4's equivalent test for the supervisor-driven path.
docs/plan/plan.md-4398-- Regression test: `cp`-overwriting the spawn-path binary's content in place (no re-exec) is detected by the 11.3 check and produces a `spawn_path.modified_in_place` event.
docs/plan/plan.md-4399-
docs/plan/plan.md-4400-### 11.6 Deployment
docs/plan/plan.md:4401:- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`). 11.1 specifically should be validated with its own canary fixture (simulate a spawn-path `mv` mid-canary-run) before promotion, since it patches part of the hot-reload machinery it depends on.
docs/plan/plan.md-4402-
docs/plan/plan.md-4403-## Exit criteria
docs/plan/plan.md-4404-- A worker whose spawn-path binary is replaced via `mv` while it's running recovers on its own within one loop cycle, with no permanent stall and no operator intervention.
docs/plan/plan.md-4405-- `needle upgrade` never installs an unvalidated release — a failing canary against a manually-triggered upgrade leaves the previous version running, same guarantee Phase 9 provides for the automatic path.
docs/plan/plan.md-4406-- An operator who runs `cp`/`mv` directly against a spawn-path binary sees an explicit warning (via `needle doctor` or telemetry) rather than silent, delayed, hard-to-diagnose session disruption.

docs/plan/plan.md-4650-Three independent defects stack:
docs/plan/plan.md-4651-
docs/plan/plan.md:4652:1. **The OTel Resource never reaches the wire.** `src/telemetry/otlp.rs` interposes four resilience wrappers (`ResilientHttp/GrpcLogExporter`, `ResilientHttp/GrpcSpanExporter`) that implement `export()` and nothing else. `LogExporter::set_resource` and `SpanExporter::set_resource` are **defaulted no-ops** on the SDK traits, so each wrapper silently absorbs the Resource that `SdkLoggerProvider::build()` pushes down and never forwards it to the inner `opentelemetry_otlp` exporter. A raw capture of the deployed 0.3.1 binary's `/v1/logs` payload contains **zero** resource attributes — no `service.name`, no `service.version`, no `deployment.cluster`, no `needle.worker.pool`, none of the `needle.*` trio. `OtlpSink::build_resource()` is correct; its output is discarded one hop before the socket. Metrics are unaffected (`MetricExporter` is not wrapped), which is why `deployment.cluster` — injected by the *collector*, not by NEEDLE — is the one dashboard field that works.
docs/plan/plan.md-4653-
docs/plan/plan.md-4654-2. **`TelemetryEvent.workspace` is a dead field.** It is declared (`telemetry/mod.rs:71`), documented in the telemetry module spec above, filterable (`mod.rs:4023`), read by `OtlpSink::emit_log` — and hardcoded to `None` at both emit sites (`mod.rs:3323`, `mod.rs:3488`). The dashboard's *first* choice for `repo` is exactly this attribute.
docs/plan/plan.md-4655-
docs/plan/plan.md-4656-3. **Identity is resolved once at boot, from config, onto an immutable Resource.** `worker_telemetry_identity()` (`cli/mod.rs:849`) reads `config.agent.default` and `config.workspace.default`. But `needle run -w` states in its own help text that the home workspace is "NOT an exclusive scope" — the Explore strand roams, and model selection is per-dispatch whenever `agent.routing` is set. A Resource attribute cannot track either. Fixing (1) alone would make `Repo` confidently wrong rather than blank.
docs/plan/plan.md-4657-

docs/plan/plan.md-4659-
docs/plan/plan.md:4660:### 17.1 Forward `set_resource` through every exporter wrapper
docs/plan/plan.md:4661:- Implement `set_resource` on `ResilientHttpLogExporter`, `ResilientGrpcLogExporter`, `ResilientHttpSpanExporter`, and `ResilientGrpcSpanExporter`, delegating to the inner exporter via `Arc::get_mut` (unique at provider-build time, which is when the SDK calls it). WARN if the unique reference cannot be obtained — a silently resource-less exporter is the bug being fixed.
docs/plan/plan.md:4662:- **Normative rule:** a wrapper interposed on an OTel SDK exporter trait must implement *every* method of that trait, including defaulted no-ops. `export()` alone is never a complete implementation.

docs/plan/plan.md-4694-# Phase 18: Configuration Hot-Reload at the Cycle Boundary
docs/plan/plan.md-4695-
docs/plan/plan.md-4696-**Status:** proposed (ADR-017).
docs/plan/plan.md-4697-
docs/plan/plan.md:4698:**Goal:** make a configuration change take effect on a running worker without a restart, at the boundary where it is already safe to change things. Driven by the 2026-08-21 fleet-wide OTLP migration: flipping one boolean (`telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled`) required draining and relaunching all fifteen ex44 workers — ~55 minutes of wall clock, bounded by whatever each worker's in-flight dispatch happened to be doing, with every drained worker releasing its claimed bead. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-017](../adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md).
docs/plan/plan.md-4699-
docs/plan/plan.md-4700-The runtime is built to make this impossible today, in three distinct ways:
docs/plan/plan.md-4701-
docs/plan/plan.md-4702-1. **Config is a boot-time snapshot.** `Config`'s own doc comment says "Loaded once at boot, immutable during a session." `Worker::new` builds `Telemetry`, `StrandRunner`, `PromptBuilder`, `Dispatcher`, `OutcomeHandler`, `HealthMonitor`, and `RateLimiter` from that snapshot and holds them for the process lifetime.
docs/plan/plan.md:4703:2. **The tracing subscriber is a one-shot global.** `init_tracing_subscriber` installs the OTLP layer via `tracing_subscriber::registry()....try_init()`. A process that booted without a reload handle can never acquire one.
docs/plan/plan.md-4704-3. **Unapplicable config is discarded silently.** `telemetry` is in `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS`, so a workspace `.needle.yaml` enabling OTLP is parsed, warned once, and dropped. The fleet ran for days on a config file that read as correct.
docs/plan/plan.md-4705-
docs/plan/plan.md:4706:The safe seam already exists: `check_hot_reload()` runs after `LOGGING`, "between dispatch cycles, never mid-claim, ensuring no bead is left in_progress." Config reload is the same problem with a smaller blast radius.
docs/plan/plan.md-4707-
docs/plan/plan.md:4708:**That seam's history is itself a requirement.** `check_hot_reload` was `#[allow(dead_code)]` with no call site anywhere from 2026-03-21 until ~2026-08-16 (`needle-eea03800`) — five months during which its doc comment claimed it ran between LOGGING and SELECTING, and every "hot-reload" deploy was really a manual kill-and-relaunch. It is live now (21 `binary.freshness.exit` events as of 2026-08-21), but that is days of evidence, not months. A reload mechanism that is *documented* to run is not one that runs: Phase 18 must assert the config check actually executes, and fail if the call site is ever dropped.
docs/plan/plan.md-4709-
docs/plan/plan.md-4710-## Decisions locked
docs/plan/plan.md-4711-
docs/plan/plan.md-4712-An implementer will hit each of these forks; the plan decides them so no mid-build ADR is needed.
docs/plan/plan.md-4713-
docs/plan/plan.md:4714:- **Trigger = polled mtime+hash at the cycle boundary**, gated by `worker.config_reload_check_interval_secs` (`0` = disabled, and is the default until the feature has fleet time). *Because* it mirrors `check_hot_reload`'s existing binary-hash check and adds no dependency. *Rejected:* a `notify` file watcher (new dep, new async task, and it must defer to the boundary anyway). *Enforced by* 18.2.
docs/plan/plan.md:4715:- **SIGHUP must NOT be the trigger.** *Because* `install_unix_signal_handlers` already registers `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`/`SIGHUP` onto the shutdown flag, deliberately — a killed tmux session delivers SIGHUP, and the handler exists so the worker can release its bead and emit `worker.stopped` rather than die silently. Repurposing it turns every tmux teardown into a reload. *Revisit if* the shutdown handler ever stops covering SIGHUP.
docs/plan/plan.md-4716-- **Reload applies only between dispatch cycles.** *Because* a worker in `Building`/`Dispatching`/`Executing`/`Handling` holds a bead, and changing `agent.timeout` or an adapter under a running dispatch produces an outcome attributable to neither config. *Enforced by* 18.2 + the test in 18.8.
docs/plan/plan.md:4717:- **Three declared tiers, written as a table in code, not inferred.** *Because* an untiered atomic swap reads as though everything is reloadable and would silently no-op for immutable keys — recreating the `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` failure that caused this work. *Enforced by* 18.1.
docs/plan/plan.md:4718:- **Validate before swap; a reload may never fail closed.** *Because* polled reload reaches every worker within one interval, so a bad edit is fleet-wide and simultaneous — strictly worse than the restart-only status quo unless validation is a hard gate. A config problem must degrade telemetry, never remove a worker. *Enforced by* 18.3.
docs/plan/plan.md:4719:- **The `reload::Layer` seam is installed unconditionally at boot, including when OTLP is off.** *Because* `try_init()` is one-shot; installing the seam only when OTLP is already enabled means turning OTLP *on* still needs a restart — the exact situation this phase exists to remove, undiscoverable until tried on a live fleet. *Enforced by* 18.5.
docs/plan/plan.md:4720:- **A reload never tears down a working exporter.** *Because* a reload cannot introduce a new environment variable into a running process, so a rebuild needing an absent `env:` header must keep the old exporter and report. *Enforced by* 18.5.
docs/plan/plan.md-4721-
docs/plan/plan.md-4722-## Changes
docs/plan/plan.md-4723-
docs/plan/plan.md:4724:### 18.1 Declare a reload tier for every config key
docs/plan/plan.md:4725:- A table in `src/config/` mapping each key path to **Tier A (live)**, **Tier B (rebuild)**, or **Tier C (restart-required)**.
docs/plan/plan.md:4726:- Tier A: `worker.idle_*`, `worker.max_claim_retries`, `agent.timeout`, `budget.*`, strand thresholds — read live off `self.config`, effective next cycle with no rebuild.
docs/plan/plan.md:4727:- Tier B: `telemetry.*`, `strands.*`, `prompt.*`, `agent.adapters_dir`, `limits.*`, gates/verification — owned by a component built in `Worker::new`.
docs/plan/plan.md-4728-- Tier C: worker identity/`qualified_id`, `workspace.home`, `bead_cli.backend`, tokio runtime, tracing-stack shape.
docs/plan/plan.md-4729-- **Normative rule:** a new config key must be assigned a tier in the same change that introduces it. An unclassified key is a compile-time failure, not a runtime surprise.
docs/plan/plan.md-4730-
docs/plan/plan.md:4731:### 18.2 Cycle-boundary reload check
docs/plan/plan.md:4732:- `check_config_reload()` alongside `check_hot_reload()` after `do_log()`, gated by `worker.config_reload_check_interval_secs`.
docs/plan/plan.md-4733-- Detect via mtime plus content hash of the resolved global config path (mtime alone is not sufficient — an editor that rewrites in place with a preserved mtime would be missed).
docs/plan/plan.md:4734:- Per-section hashing so 18.4 can rebuild only the components whose own subtree changed.
docs/plan/plan.md-4735-
docs/plan/plan.md-4736-### 18.3 Validate-before-swap, and never fail closed
docs/plan/plan.md-4737-- Run `ConfigLoader::validate` against the candidate before any swap.
docs/plan/plan.md:4738:- On error: keep the running config, emit `config.reload.rejected` with the errors, WARN, continue. Never propagate a reload error into the worker's `Result` path — that is how a config problem becomes a dead worker.
docs/plan/plan.md-4739-- The swap itself is all-or-nothing: no half-applied configuration is ever observable.
docs/plan/plan.md-4740-
docs/plan/plan.md:4741:### 18.4 Rebuild Tier-B components
docs/plan/plan.md:4742:- Reconstruct only components whose config subtree changed: `StrandRunner`, `PromptBuilder`, `Dispatcher` (adapter reload), `RateLimiter`, `OutcomeHandler`.
docs/plan/plan.md:4743:- Each rebuild is fallible and isolated: a component that fails to rebuild keeps its previous instance and reports, rather than leaving the worker with a missing component.
docs/plan/plan.md-4744-
docs/plan/plan.md-4745-### 18.5 Reload-safe telemetry
docs/plan/plan.md:4746:- Wrap the OTLP tracing layer in `tracing_subscriber::reload::Layer` at boot **unconditionally**, wrapping a no-op layer when OTLP is disabled. `reload` is not feature-gated in the pinned `tracing-subscriber` 0.3.23 — no new dependency.
docs/plan/plan.md-4747-- Make the telemetry writer thread's sink set swappable. The thread currently owns `Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>` for its lifetime (`PendingWriter`); add a control message on the existing channel so sinks can be replaced without tearing down the writer or losing queued events.
docs/plan/plan.md:4748:- Re-resolve `env:`-prefixed header values from the process environment on rebuild. If a required header is absent, keep the existing exporter and emit `config.reload.restart_required` — never replace a working exporter with a dead one. Header values never reach a log, event, or error message.
docs/plan/plan.md-4749-
docs/plan/plan.md-4750-### 18.6 Report what cannot be applied
docs/plan/plan.md:4751:- A Tier-C key change emits `config.reload.restart_required` naming the keys, plus a WARN.
docs/plan/plan.md-4752-- The same treatment for a workspace `.needle.yaml` carrying a `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` section — currently a single WARN into a log nobody reads.
docs/plan/plan.md-4753-
docs/plan/plan.md-4754-### 18.7 Observability
docs/plan/plan.md:4755:- Events: `config.reload.detected`, `config.reload.applied` (with the changed key paths), `config.reload.rejected`, `config.reload.restart_required`.
docs/plan/plan.md:4756:- `needle config --dump --show-source` must reflect the **live** config of a running worker, including a reload generation counter, so an operator can confirm what a worker is actually running rather than what the file says.
docs/plan/plan.md-4757-
docs/plan/plan.md-4758-### 18.8 Tests
docs/plan/plan.md:4759:- A reload requested mid-dispatch is not applied until the cycle boundary; a dispatch launched under the old config completes under it.
docs/plan/plan.md:4760:- An invalid candidate config leaves the worker running on the previous config and emits `config.reload.rejected` — the worker must still be alive at the end of the test.
docs/plan/plan.md:4761:- OTLP toggles false→true and true→false on a running worker, asserted at the transport seam (per the ADR-016 rule: assert on what the exporter is handed, not on a builder's return value).
docs/plan/plan.md-4762-- A Tier-C key change reports and does not silently no-op.
docs/plan/plan.md:4763:- A rebuild whose `env:` header is absent keeps the previous exporter.
docs/plan/plan.md:4764:- **The reload check actually executes.** A test that fails if `check_config_reload()` loses its call site or is never reached from the state machine — the `needle-eea03800` failure mode, where a documented-as-running mechanism was dead code for five months.
docs/plan/plan.md-4765-
docs/plan/plan.md-4766-## Exit criteria
docs/plan/plan.md-4767-- `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled` can be flipped on a running worker and traces appear at the collector without the process restarting.
docs/plan/plan.md:4768:- No reload is ever applied while a bead is claimed; no bead is released by a reload.
docs/plan/plan.md:4769:- An invalid config edit leaves every worker running, with `config.reload.rejected` emitted — verified by editing the live fleet config to something invalid and observing zero worker exits.
docs/plan/plan.md:4770:- Changing a Tier-C key produces a named `config.reload.restart_required` rather than silence.
docs/plan/plan.md:4771:- `needle config --dump --show-source` against a running worker reflects a post-reload value, not the boot-time snapshot.
docs/plan/plan.md-4772-- The 2026-08-21 migration is reproducible as a config edit: enabling OTLP fleet-wide costs one interval, not a fifteen-worker drain.

docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-34-1. **The cost of a config change is a fleet rollover.** Not a restart of one
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-35-   process — a staged drain of every worker, each releasing a claimed bead.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-36-2. **A config flip is *armed*, not inert.** needle ≥0.4 fails closed when
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-37-   `otlp_sink.enabled` is true and `NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION` is absent:
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-38-   `init_tracing_subscriber` → `build_http_providers()?` propagates and the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:39:   worker refuses to boot. Editing the file while a header-less fleet runs does
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-40-   not do nothing — it means the *next* restart of each worker kills it.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-41-3. **Config that cannot apply is silently discarded.** `telemetry` sits in
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-42-   `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS`, so `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` in a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-43-   workspace `.needle.yaml` is parsed, warned to a log nobody reads, and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-44-   dropped. The fleet ran for days with a config file that looked correct.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-45-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:46:The seam this needs already exists: `check_hot_reload()` runs after the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-47-`LOGGING` state, described in-code as running "between dispatch cycles, never
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:48:mid-claim, ensuring no bead is left in_progress." Configuration reload is the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-49-same problem with a smaller blast radius.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-50-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-51-**But that seam's own history is a warning, not a reassurance.**
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:52:`check_hot_reload` carried `#[allow(dead_code)]` and had **no call site
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-53-anywhere** from its introduction on 2026-03-21 until it was wired in around
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-54-2026-08-16 (`needle-eea03800`) — for five months, while its doc comment stated
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-55-it was "called between LOGGING and SELECTING." Every deploy in that window was
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:56:a manual kill-and-relaunch that people believed was a hot-reload. It is
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-57-genuinely live now (21 `binary.freshness.exit` events as of 2026-08-21), so the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-58-boundary is real and exercised — but it has days of production evidence, not
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-59-months.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-60-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:61:The lesson transfers directly: a reload mechanism that is *documented* to run is
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:62:not a reload mechanism that runs. Phase 18 must prove the config check actually
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-63-executes, with a test that fails if the call site disappears — not inherit the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-64-assumption that wiring it once means it stays wired.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-65-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-66-## Decision
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-67-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-68-### 1. Reload is evaluated only at the existing cycle boundary
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-69-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:70:The reload check runs where `check_hot_reload()` runs — after `do_log()`,
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-71-between dispatch cycles, never mid-claim and never mid-dispatch. A worker in
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-72-`Building`/`Dispatching`/`Executing`/`Handling` holds a bead; nothing about its
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-73-configuration may change underneath it.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-74-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:75:**Rejected:** applying a reload the moment it is detected. It would let
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-76-`agent.timeout` or an adapter definition change while a dispatch that was
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-77-launched under the old value is still running, producing outcomes attributable
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-78-to neither config.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-79-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-80-### 2. The trigger is a polled mtime+hash check, interval-gated
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-81-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:82:Gated by a new `worker.config_reload_check_interval_secs` (`0` disables, and is
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:83:the default until the feature has fleet time). This mirrors `check_hot_reload`'s
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-84-existing binary-hash check exactly, and adds **no new dependency**.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-85-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-86-**Rejected — SIGHUP.** SIGHUP is already bound to the shutdown flag:
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-87-`install_unix_signal_handlers` registers `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, and `SIGHUP`
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-88-together, deliberately, because a killed tmux session delivers SIGHUP to the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-89-worker and the handler exists so the worker can release its bead and emit
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-90-`worker.stopped` instead of dying silently. Repurposing SIGHUP would turn every
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:91:tmux teardown into a reload. This constraint is not obvious from the outside and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-92-is the single most likely wrong turn for an implementer here.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-93-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-94-**Rejected — a file watcher (`notify`).** A new dependency and a new async task,
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-95-and it still cannot apply anything at the instant it fires; it would have to
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-96-defer to the cycle boundary regardless. The poll is strictly simpler for the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-97-same delivered behaviour.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-98-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:99:### 3. Every config key has a declared reload tier
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-100-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-101-The tier is declared in code as a table, not inferred:
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-102-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-103-| Tier | Meaning | Examples |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-104-|---|---|---|
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:105:| **A — live** | Swap `self.config`; effective next cycle, no rebuild. | `worker.idle_*`, `worker.max_claim_retries`, `agent.timeout`, `budget.*`, strand thresholds |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:106:| **B — rebuild** | Component reconstructed from the new config at the boundary. | `telemetry.*` sinks, `strands.*`, `prompt.*`, `agent.adapters_dir`, `limits.*`, gates/verification |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-107-| **C — immutable** | Requires a restart. | worker identity / `qualified_id`, `workspace.home`, `bead_cli.backend`, the tokio runtime, the shape of the tracing subscriber stack |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-108-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-109-**Rejected:** a single atomic swap of the whole `Config` with no tiering. It
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:110:reads as if everything is reloadable, and would silently no-op for the Tier-C
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-111-keys — recreating the exact `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` failure that caused this
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-112-work.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-113-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:114:### 4. Validate before swap; a reload may never fail closed
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-115-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-116-The candidate config is validated with the existing `ConfigLoader::validate`
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-117-before anything is swapped. On any error the running config is kept, a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:118:`config.reload.rejected` event is emitted with the errors, and the worker
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-119-continues on its current configuration.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-120-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:121:This is non-negotiable and is the direct lesson of the OTLP header: a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-122-configuration problem must degrade telemetry, never remove a worker. A typo in a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:123:YAML file must not be able to take down the fleet — and with polled reload, a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-124-bad edit would otherwise reach every worker simultaneously within one interval,
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-125-which is *worse* than the restart-only status quo.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-126-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:127:### 5. The reload seam is installed unconditionally at boot
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-128-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:129:The OTLP tracing layer is wrapped in `tracing_subscriber::reload::Layer` from
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-130-the first moment of process start — **including when OTLP is disabled**, where
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-131-it wraps a no-op layer.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-132-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-133-This is the load-bearing decision. `try_init()` is one-shot: a process that
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:134:booted without a reload handle can never acquire one. If the seam is installed
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-135-only when OTLP is already enabled, then turning OTLP *on* still requires a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-136-restart — which is precisely the situation this ADR exists to eliminate, and it
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:137:would not be discovered until someone tried it on a live fleet. `reload` is not
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-138-feature-gated in the pinned `tracing-subscriber` 0.3.23, so this costs no new
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-139-dependency.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-140-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-141-### 6. Changes that cannot be applied are reported, never silently ignored
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-142-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:143:A Tier-C key changing produces a `config.reload.restart_required` event naming
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-144-the keys, and a WARN. The same applies to a workspace `.needle.yaml` carrying a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-145-`NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` section. Silence is what let the fleet run for days on a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-146-config file that read as correct.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-147-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:148:### 7. Secrets are re-resolved, never re-logged, and never tear down a live exporter
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-149-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:150:`env:`-prefixed header values are re-resolved from the process environment on a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:151:Tier-B telemetry rebuild. A reload **cannot** introduce a new environment
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:152:variable into a running process, so if a rebuild would need a header the process
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:153:does not have, the existing exporter is kept and the condition reported. A
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:154:reload must never convert a working exporter into a dead one. Header values are
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-155-never written to a log, an event, or an error message.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-156-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-157-## Consequences
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-158-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-159-- Enabling or disabling OTLP, changing timeouts, thresholds, gates, or prompts
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-160-  becomes a file edit plus at most one check interval — no drain, no released
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-161-  beads, no rollover.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-162-- A restart remains required for identity, `workspace.home`, bead backend, and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-163-  runtime-shaped concerns. That set is now explicit rather than discovered.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:164:- Tier-B rebuilds add bounded latency at the cycle boundary. Mitigated by
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:165:  hashing per config section and rebuilding only components whose own subtree
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-166-  changed.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-167-- The blast radius of a bad config edit grows from "the next worker to restart"
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-168-  to "every worker within one interval". Decision 4 is what makes that safe, and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-169-  is the reason validation is a hard gate rather than a warning.
