   392	
   393	/// OTLP sink implementing the telemetry Sink trait.
   394	///
   395	/// Wraps the OpenTelemetry SDK providers and translates TelemetryEvent
   396	/// into traces, metrics, and logs per the semantic mapping.
   397	///
   398	/// ## Resilience
   399	///
   400	/// The OTel SDK's batch processors provide bounded queues that drop
   401	/// oldest items when full. Export failures are logged at WARN level
   402	/// but do not crash the worker. Shutdown has a 5-second timeout.
   403	#[derive(Clone)]
   404	pub struct OtlpSink {
   405	    /// Tracer provider for trace export.
   406	    tracer_provider: Arc<SdkTracerProvider>,
   407	    /// Meter provider for metric export.
   408	    meter_provider: Arc<SdkMeterProvider>,
   409	    /// Logger provider for log export.
   410	    logger_provider: Arc<SdkLoggerProvider>,
   411	    /// Cached metric instruments.
   412	    metrics: Metrics,
   413	    /// File sink for emitting drop events (never to OTLP, to avoid recursion).
   414	    /// Wrapped in Arc so it can be shared with the drop monitor task.
   415	    file_sink: Option<Arc<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>>,
   416	    /// Worker ID for drop events.
   417	    worker_id: String,
   418	    /// Session ID for drop events.
   419	    session_id: String,
   420	    /// Next sequence number for drop events.
   421	    next_drop_sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   422	    /// Observable state for gauges (heartbeat.age, queue.depth).
   423	    observable_state: Arc<ObservableState>,
   424	    /// Drop monitor task handle - kept alive to ensure the task runs.
   425	    _drop_monitor_handle: Arc<DropMonitorHandle>,
   426	}
   427	
   428	/// Handle to keep the drop monitor task alive.
   429	///
   430	/// Uses an atomic flag to signal shutdown to the monitor task.
   431	#[allow(dead_code)]
   432	struct DropMonitorHandle {
   433	    shutdown: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   434	}
   435	
   436	#[allow(dead_code)]
   437	impl DropMonitorHandle {
   438	    fn new() -> Self {
   439	        Self {
   440	            shutdown: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0)),
   441	        }
   442	    }
   443	
   444	    fn is_shutdown(&self) -> bool {
   445	        self.shutdown.load(Ordering::Relaxed) != 0
   446	    }
   447	
   448	    fn shutdown(&self) {
   449	        self.shutdown.store(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
   450	    }
   451	}
   452	
   453	/// Sequence number atomic for drop events.
   454	#[derive(Clone)]
   455	#[allow(dead_code)]
   456	struct DropSequence(Arc<AtomicU64>);
   457	
   458	/// State for observable gauges.
   459	#[derive(Default)]
   460	struct ObservableState {
   461	    /// Last heartbeat timestamp (UNIX epoch seconds).
   462	    last_heartbeat_secs: AtomicU64,
   463	    /// Queue depth per priority level (sampled at strand evaluation).
   464	    /// Maps priority -> count.
   465	    queue_depth_by_priority: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<u8, AtomicU64>>>,
   466	}
   467	
   468	/// Cached metric instruments for efficient recording.
   469	#[derive(Clone)]
   470	#[allow(dead_code)]
   471	struct Metrics {
   472	    /// UpDownCounter: `needle.workers.active`
   473	    workers_active: UpDownCounter<i64>,
   474	    /// Counter: `needle.beads.claimed`
   475	    beads_claimed: Counter<u64>,
   476	    /// Counter: `needle.beads.completed`
   477	    beads_completed: Counter<u64>,
   478	    /// Histogram: `needle.beads.duration`
   479	    bead_duration: Histogram<f64>,
   480	    /// Counter: `needle.claim.attempts`
   481	    claim_attempts: Counter<u64>,
   482	    /// Histogram: `needle.strand.duration`
   483	    strand_duration: Histogram<f64>,
   484	    /// Histogram: `needle.agent.duration`
   485	    agent_duration: Histogram<f64>,
   486	    /// Counter: `needle.agent.tokens.input`
   487	    tokens_input: Counter<u64>,
   488	    /// Counter: `needle.agent.tokens.output`
   489	    tokens_output: Counter<u64>,
   490	    /// Counter: `needle.cost.usd`
   491	    cost_usd: Counter<f64>,
   492	    /// ObservableGauge: `needle.heartbeat.age`
   493	    heartbeat_age: ObservableGauge<u64>,
   494	    /// ObservableGauge: `needle.queue.depth`
   495	    queue_depth: ObservableGauge<u64>,
   496	    /// UpDownCounter: `needle.peers.stale`
   497	    peers_stale: UpDownCounter<i64>,
   498	    /// Counter: `needle.mitosis.children_created`
   499	    mitosis_children_created: Counter<u64>,
   500	}
   501	
   502	impl OtlpSink {
   503	    /// Create a new OTLP sink from configuration.
   504	    ///
   505	    /// Initializes the OpenTelemetry SDK with batch processors for
   506	    /// non-blocking export of all three signals.
   507	    ///
   508	    /// The `file_sink` parameter is used to emit shutdown timeout events
   509	    /// when the flush takes longer than 5 seconds.
   510	    ///
   511	    /// The `agent`, `model`, `provider`, and `workspace` parameters are optional resource
   512	    /// attributes for OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
   513	    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   514	    pub fn new(
   515	        worker_id: String,
   516	        session_id: String,
   517	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   518	        file_sink: Option<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>,
   519	        agent: Option<&str>,
   520	        model: Option<&str>,
   521	        provider: Option<&str>,
   522	        workspace: Option<&str>,
   523	    ) -> Result<Self> {
   524	        // Build resource attributes from config + computed attributes
   525	        let resource = Self::build_resource(
   526	            &worker_id,
   527	            &session_id,
   528	            config,
   529	            agent,
   530	            model,
   531	            provider,
   532	            workspace,
   533	        )?;
   534	
   535	        // Create drop sequence atomic and monitor channel
   536	        let next_drop_sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
   537	        let (drop_tx, drop_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<DropEvent>();
   538	
   539	        // Wrap file_sink in Arc so it can be shared with drop monitor task
   540	        let file_sink_arc = file_sink.map(Arc::new);
   541	
   542	        // Drop monitor task spawn deferred to avoid runtime initialization issues
   543	        // The drop channel is created but the monitor task is not spawned during init
   544	        let _file_sink_for_monitor = file_sink_arc.clone();
   545	        let _worker_id_clone = worker_id.clone();
   546	        let _session_id_clone = session_id.clone();
   547	        let _next_drop_seq_clone = next_drop_sequence.clone();
   548	        let _drop_rx = drop_rx;
   549	        // Note: The drop monitor task would be spawned later in the worker's main runtime
   550	
   551	        // Build exporters based on protocol
   552	        let (tracer_provider, meter_provider, logger_provider) = match config.protocol.as_str() {
   553	            "grpc" => Self::build_grpc_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
   554	            "http" | "http/protobuf" => Self::build_http_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
   555	            other => anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'"),
   556	        };
   557	
   558	        // Build metric instruments
   559	        let meter = meter_provider.meter("needle");
   560	        let observable_state = Arc::new(ObservableState::default());
   561	
   562	        // Clone Arc for each callback (they need to outlive this function)
   563	        let heartbeat_state = observable_state.clone();
   564	        let worker_id_for_callback = worker_id.clone();
   565	
   566	        // Register observable gauges with callbacks
   567	        let heartbeat_age = meter
   568	            .u64_observable_gauge("needle.heartbeat.age")
   569	            .with_unit("s")
   570	            .with_description("Seconds since last heartbeat emitted by this worker")
   571	            .with_callback(move |observer| {
   572	                let now = SystemTime::now()
   573	                    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
   574	                    .map(|d| d.as_secs())
   575	                    .unwrap_or(0);
   576	                let last = heartbeat_state.last_heartbeat_secs.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
   577	                if last > 0 && now > last {
   578	                    observer.observe(
   579	                        now - last,
   580	                        &[KeyValue::new("worker_id", worker_id_for_callback.clone())],
   581	                    );
   582	                }
   583	            })
   584	            .build();
   585	
   586	        // Clone Arc for queue depth callback
   587	        let queue_state = observable_state.clone();
   588	        // Capture workspace for queue depth attribute (bounded cardinality: one per worker)
   589	        let workspace_attr = workspace.map(workspace_label);
   590	
   591	        let queue_depth = meter
   592	            .u64_observable_gauge("needle.queue.depth")
   593	            .with_unit("{bead}")
   594	            .with_description("Open beads visible to this worker (sampled at strand evaluation)")
   595	            .with_callback(move |observer| {
   596	                // Observe queue depth for each priority level
   597	                let guard = queue_state.queue_depth_by_priority.lock().unwrap();
   598	                for (priority, count) in guard.iter() {
   599	                    // Build attributes vector with priority and optional workspace
   600	                    let mut attrs = vec![KeyValue::new("priority", i64::from(*priority))];
   601	                    if let Some(ref ws) = workspace_attr {
   602	                        attrs.push(KeyValue::new("workspace", ws.clone()));
   603	                    }
   604	                    observer.observe(count.load(Ordering::Relaxed), &attrs);
   605	                }
   606	            })
   607	            .build();
   608	
   609	        let metrics = Metrics {
   610	            workers_active: meter
   611	                .i64_up_down_counter("needle.workers.active")
   612	                .with_unit("{worker}")
   613	                .with_description("Current live worker count")
   614	                .build(),
   615	            beads_claimed: meter
   616	                .u64_counter("needle.beads.claimed")
   617	                .with_unit("{bead}")
   618	                .with_description("Successful bead claims")
   619	                .build(),
   620	            beads_completed: meter
   720	                    event_type: "telemetry.otlp.dropped".to_string(),
   721	                    worker_id: worker_id.clone(),
   722	                    session_id: session_id.clone(),
   723	                    sequence,
   724	                    bead_id: None,
   725	                    workspace: None,
   726	                    duration_ms: None,
   727	                    data: serde_json::Value::Object(data),
   728	                    trace_id: None,
   729	                    span_id: None,
   730	                };
   731	
   732	                // Emit to file sink - ignore errors to avoid recursion
   733	                let _ = catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
   734	                    if let Err(e) = (**sink).accept(&event) {
   735	                        warn!("failed to write OTLP drop event to file sink: {e}");
   736	                    }
   737	                }));
   738	            }
   739	        }
   740	    }
   741	
   742	    /// Build the OTel Resource with config and computed attributes.
   743	    ///
   744	    /// Merges three layers (lowest → highest precedence):
   745	    /// 1. OTel defaults (service.name = "needle", schema url)
   746	    /// 2. Computed attributes (set by NEEDLE at runtime)
   747	    /// 3. Config attributes (from telemetry.otlp.resource_attributes)
   748	    ///
   749	    /// Reserved keys `service.name` and `service.instance.id` cannot be overridden
   750	    /// via config - attempting to do so will return an error.
   751	    pub fn build_resource(
   752	        worker_id: &str,
   753	        session_id: &str,
   754	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   755	        agent: Option<&str>,
   756	        model: Option<&str>,
   757	        provider: Option<&str>,
   758	        workspace: Option<&str>,
   759	    ) -> Result<Resource> {
   760	        // Reserved keys that cannot be overridden via config
   761	        const RESERVED_KEYS: &[&str] = &["service.name", "service.instance.id"];
   762	
   763	        let mut builder = Resource::builder().with_attributes([
   764	            KeyValue::new("service.name", "needle"),
   765	            KeyValue::new("service.namespace", config.service_namespace.clone()),
   766	            KeyValue::new("service.version", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")),
   767	            KeyValue::new("service.instance.id", worker_id.to_string()),
   768	            KeyValue::new("needle.session_id", session_id.to_string()),
   769	        ]);
   770	
   771	        // Add hostname from OS
   772	        if let Some(hostname) = gethostname::gethostname().to_str() {
   773	            builder = builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new("host.name", hostname.to_string())]);
   774	        }
   775	
   776	        // Add process PID
   777	        builder =
   778	            builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new("process.pid", std::process::id().to_string())]);
   779	
   780	        // Add computed needle.* attributes if provided
   781	        if let Some(agent_value) = agent {
   782	            builder =
   783	                builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new("needle.agent", agent_value.to_string())]);
   784	        }
   785	        if let Some(model_value) = model {
   786	            builder =
   787	                builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new("needle.model", model_value.to_string())]);
   788	        }
   789	        if let Some(provider_value) = provider {
   790	            builder = builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(
   791	                "needle.model.provider",
   792	                provider_value.to_string(),
   793	            )]);
   794	        }
   795	        if let Some(workspace_value) = workspace {
   796	            builder = builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(
   797	                "needle.workspace",
   798	                workspace_label(workspace_value),
   799	            )]);
   800	        }
   801	
   802	        // Add resource attributes from config (KEY=VALUE pairs)
   803	        // Validate that reserved keys are not being overridden
   804	        for attr_str in &config.resource_attributes {
   805	            if let Some((key, value)) = attr_str.split_once('=') {
   806	                if RESERVED_KEYS.contains(&key) {
   807	                    anyhow::bail!(
   808	                        "cannot override reserved resource attribute '{key}' via config. \
   809	                         Reserved keys are: service.name, service.instance.id"
   810	                    );
   811	                }
   812	                builder =
   813	                    builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(key.to_string(), value.to_string())]);
   814	            }
   815	        }
   816	
   817	        // Detect SDK-provided attributes (telemetry.sdk.*)
   818	        let resource = builder
   819	            .with_detector(Box::new(TelemetryResourceDetector))
   820	            .with_detector(Box::new(SdkProvidedResourceDetector))
   821	            .build();
   822	
   823	        Ok(resource)
   824	    }
   825	
   826	    /// Build providers using gRPC transport (tonic).
   827	    pub fn build_grpc_providers(
   828	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   829	        resource: &Resource,
   830	        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
   831	    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)> {
   832	        let metadata = Self::build_grpc_metadata(config)?;
   833	        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);
   834	
   835	        // Import the tonic-specific exporters
   836	        use opentelemetry_otlp::WithTonicConfig;
   837	        use opentelemetry_otlp::{LogExporter, SpanExporter, WithExportConfig};
   838	
   839	        // Build the transport exporters, then use the same provider path as the
   840	        // transport-seam tests below.
   841	        let base_span_exporter = SpanExporter::builder()
   842	            .with_tonic()
   843	            .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone())
   844	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   845	            .with_metadata(metadata.clone())
   846	            .build()?;
   847	        let base_log_exporter = LogExporter::builder()
   848	            .with_tonic()
   849	            .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone())
   850	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   851	            .with_metadata(metadata.clone())
   852	            .build()?;
   853	
   854	        Self::build_grpc_providers_with_exporters_inner(
   855	            config,
   856	            resource,
   857	            drop_tx,
   858	            metadata,
   859	            base_span_exporter,
   860	            base_log_exporter,
   861	        )
   862	    }
   863	
   864	    /// Build gRPC providers with transport exporters supplied by the caller.
   865	    ///
   866	    /// This is the transport seam used by tests: the provider construction,
   867	    /// batch processors, resource assignment, and resilient wrappers are the
   868	    /// same path as [`Self::build_grpc_providers`], while the exporter at the
   869	    /// transport boundary can capture the resource it receives.
   870	    #[doc(hidden)]
   871	    pub fn build_grpc_providers_with_exporters<S, L>(
   872	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   873	        resource: &Resource,
   874	        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
   875	        span_exporter: S,
   876	        log_exporter: L,
   877	    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>
   878	    where
   879	        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,
   880	        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,
   881	    {
   882	        Self::build_grpc_providers_with_exporters_inner(
   883	            config,
   884	            resource,
   885	            drop_tx,
   886	            Self::build_grpc_metadata(config)?,
   887	            span_exporter,
   888	            log_exporter,
   889	        )
   890	    }
   891	
   892	    fn build_grpc_providers_with_exporters_inner<S, L>(
   893	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   894	        resource: &Resource,
   895	        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
   896	        metadata: tonic::metadata::MetadataMap,
   897	        base_span_exporter: S,
   898	        base_log_exporter: L,
   899	    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>
   900	    where
   901	        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,
   902	        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,
   903	    {
   904	        use opentelemetry_otlp::{MetricExporter, WithExportConfig, WithTonicConfig};
   905	
   906	        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);
   907	
   908	        let span_exporter = ResilientGrpcSpanExporter::new(base_span_exporter, drop_tx.clone());
   909	        let batch_span_processor = BatchSpanProcessor::builder(span_exporter).build();
   910	        let tracer_provider = SdkTracerProvider::builder()
   911	            .with_span_processor(batch_span_processor)
   912	            .with_resource(resource.clone())
   913	            .build();
   914	
   915	        let metric_exporter = MetricExporter::builder()
   916	            .with_tonic()
   917	            .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone())
   918	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   919	            .with_metadata(metadata.clone())
   920	            .build()?;
   921	        let metric_reader = PeriodicReader::builder(metric_exporter)
   922	            .with_interval(Duration::from_secs(config.metrics_interval_secs))
   923	            .build();
   924	        let meter_provider = SdkMeterProvider::builder()
   925	            .with_reader(metric_reader)
   926	            .with_resource(resource.clone())
   927	            .build();
   928	
   929	        let log_exporter = ResilientGrpcLogExporter::new(base_log_exporter, drop_tx);
   930	        let batch_log_processor = BatchLogProcessor::builder(log_exporter).build();
   931	        let logger_provider = SdkLoggerProvider::builder()
   932	            .with_log_processor(batch_log_processor)
   933	            .with_resource(resource.clone())
   934	            .build();
   935	
   936	        Ok((tracer_provider, meter_provider, logger_provider))
   937	    }
   938	
   939	    fn build_grpc_metadata(config: &OtlpSinkConfig) -> Result<tonic::metadata::MetadataMap> {
   940	        use tonic::metadata::{MetadataKey, MetadataMap, MetadataValue};
   941	
   942	        let mut metadata = MetadataMap::new();
   943	        for (key, value) in resolve_headers(&config.headers)? {
   944	            let key_val = MetadataKey::from_bytes(key.as_bytes())
   945	                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid OTLP metadata header name '{key}'"))?;
   946	            let metadata_value = MetadataValue::try_from(value.as_str())
   947	                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid value for OTLP metadata header '{key}'"))?;
   948	            metadata.insert(key_val, metadata_value);
   949	        }
   950	        Ok(metadata)
   951	    }
   952	
   953	    /// Build providers using HTTP/protobuf transport (reqwest).
   954	    pub fn build_http_providers(
   955	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   956	        resource: &Resource,
   957	        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
   958	    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)> {
   959	        use opentelemetry_otlp::WithHttpConfig;
   960	        use opentelemetry_otlp::{LogExporter, SpanExporter, WithExportConfig};
   961	
   962	        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);
   963	
   964	        let headers_map = Self::build_http_headers(config)?;
   965	
   966	        // opentelemetry-otlp only auto-appends the per-signal path
   967	        // (/v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs) when the endpoint is resolved from
   968	        // an OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT env var. When `.with_endpoint()` is
   969	        // called programmatically (as we do here, from config.endpoint), the
   970	        // SDK uses it verbatim with no path appended - so without this, every
   971	        // HTTP export request hits the collector's bare root and gets a 404.
   972	        // Confirmed live 2026-08-12 (bf-6a617): reqwest::Error { kind: Status(404,
   973	        // None), url: ".../4318/" }, and NEEDLE's own OTLP telemetry has never
   974	        // once reached the dashboard as a result.
   975	        let http_signal_endpoint =
   976	            |path: &str| format!("{}{}", config.endpoint.trim_end_matches('/'), path);
   977	
   978	        // Build the transport exporters, then use the same provider path as the
   979	        // transport-seam tests below.
   980	        let base_span_exporter = SpanExporter::builder()
   981	            .with_http()
   982	            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint("/v1/traces"))
   983	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   984	            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())
   985	            .build()?;
   986	        let base_log_exporter = LogExporter::builder()
   987	            .with_http()
   988	            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint("/v1/logs"))
   989	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   990	            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())
   991	            .build()?;
   992	
   993	        Self::build_http_providers_with_exporters_inner(
   994	            config,
   995	            resource,
   996	            drop_tx,
   997	            headers_map,
   998	            base_span_exporter,
   999	            base_log_exporter,
  1000	        )
  1001	    }
  1002	
  1003	    /// Build HTTP providers with transport exporters supplied by the caller.
  1004	    ///
  1005	    /// This is the transport seam used by tests: the provider construction,
  1006	    /// batch processors, resource assignment, and resilient wrappers are the
  1007	    /// same path as [`Self::build_http_providers`], while the exporter at the
  1008	    /// transport boundary can capture the resource it receives.
  1009	    #[doc(hidden)]
  1010	    pub fn build_http_providers_with_exporters<S, L>(
  1011	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
  1012	        resource: &Resource,
  1013	        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
  1014	        span_exporter: S,
  1015	        log_exporter: L,
  1016	    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>
  1017	    where
  1018	        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,
  1019	        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,
  1020	    {
  1021	        Self::build_http_providers_with_exporters_inner(
  1022	            config,
  1023	            resource,
  1024	            drop_tx,
  1025	            Self::build_http_headers(config)?,
  1026	            span_exporter,
  1027	            log_exporter,
  1028	        )
  1029	    }
  1030	
  1031	    fn build_http_providers_with_exporters_inner<S, L>(
  1032	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
  1033	        resource: &Resource,
  1034	        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
  1035	        headers_map: HashMap<String, String>,
  1036	        base_span_exporter: S,
  1037	        base_log_exporter: L,
  1038	    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>
  1039	    where
  1040	        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,
  1041	        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,
  1042	    {
  1043	        use opentelemetry_otlp::{MetricExporter, WithExportConfig, WithHttpConfig};
  1044	
  1045	        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);
  1046	        let http_signal_endpoint =
  1047	            |path: &str| format!("{}{}", config.endpoint.trim_end_matches('/'), path);
  1048	
  1049	        let span_exporter = ResilientHttpSpanExporter::new(base_span_exporter, drop_tx.clone());
  1050	        let batch_span_processor = BatchSpanProcessor::builder(span_exporter).build();
  1051	        let tracer_provider = SdkTracerProvider::builder()
  1052	            .with_span_processor(batch_span_processor)
  1053	            .with_resource(resource.clone())
  1054	            .build();
  1055	
  1056	        let metric_exporter = MetricExporter::builder()
  1057	            .with_http()
  1058	            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint("/v1/metrics"))
  1059	            .with_timeout(timeout)
  1060	            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())
  1061	            .build()?;
  1062	        let metric_reader = PeriodicReader::builder(metric_exporter)
  1063	            .with_interval(Duration::from_secs(config.metrics_interval_secs))
  1064	            .build();
  1065	        let meter_provider = SdkMeterProvider::builder()
  1066	            .with_reader(metric_reader)

  1084	    /// Dispatch a telemetry event to the appropriate signal.
  1085	    ///
  1086	    /// Per the semantic mapping:
  1087	    /// - Spans: bead.claim.attempted, bead.claim.succeeded, bead.claim.race_lost,
  1088	    ///   bead.claim.failed, agent.dispatched, agent.completed,
  1089	    ///   strand.evaluated, outcome.handled, bead.completed
  1090	    /// - Span events: heartbeat.emitted, build.heartbeat
  1091	    /// - Metrics: beads.completed, bead.duration, strand.duration, agent.duration, etc.
  1092	    /// - Logs: every event, providing a complete event stream for lightweight
  1093	    ///   consumers that do not query the trace backend
  1094	    fn dispatch_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {
  1095	        // Keep a complete, self-contained event feed in the log backend. Traces
  1096	        // and metrics remain the canonical analytical representations, while
  1097	        // this log copy lets dashboards reconstruct worker state without
  1098	        // joining three signal stores.
  1099	        self.emit_log(event)?;
  1100	
  1101	        match event.event_type.as_str() {
  1102	            // Metrics: worker lifecycle
  1103	            "worker.started" => {
  1104	                self.metrics.workers_active.add(1, &[]);
  1105	            }
  1106	
  1107	            "worker.stopped" => {
  1108	                self.metrics.workers_active.add(-1, &[]);
  1109	            }
  1110	
  1111	            // Events whose analytical representation is a span.
  1112	            "bead.claim.attempted" => {
  1113	                // Track claim attempts with result="attempting"
  1114	                self.metrics
  1115	                    .claim_attempts
  1116	                    .add(1, &[KeyValue::new("result", "attempting")]);
  1117	            }
  1118	
  1119	            "bead.claim.succeeded" => {
  1120	                // Track claim attempts with result="succeeded"

  3023	    /// Execute a single hook command, piping JSON to its stdin.
  3024	    ///
  3025	    /// Spawns `sh -c <command>` with the event JSON on stdin, waits for
  3026	    /// completion, and returns an error if the command exits non-zero.
  3027	    /// This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is acceptable.
  3028	    fn run_hook(command: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {
  3029	        use std::io::Write;
  3030	        use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
  3031	
  3032	        let mut child = Command::new("sh")
  3033	            .arg("-c")
  3034	            .arg(command)
  3035	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
  3036	            .stdout(Stdio::null())
  3037	            .stderr(Stdio::null())
  3038	            .spawn()
  3039	            .with_context(|| format!("failed to spawn hook: {command}"))?;
  3040	
  3041	        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
  3042	            // Best-effort write; ignore broken pipe if child exits early.
  3043	            let _ = stdin.write_all(json.as_bytes());
  3044	        }
  3045	
  3046	        // Wait for the child and check exit status.
  3047	        let status = child
  3048	            .wait()
  3049	            .with_context(|| format!("failed to wait for hook: {command}"))?;
  3050	
  3051	        if !status.success() {
  3052	            anyhow::bail!(
  3053	                "hook exited with status {}: {command}",
  3054	                status.code().unwrap_or(-1)
  3055	            );
  3056	        }
  3057	
  3058	        Ok(())
  3059	    }
  3060	
  3061	    /// HTTP POST the event JSON to a webhook URL.
  3062	    ///
  3063	    /// Sets `Content-Type: application/json` and applies a 10-second timeout.
  3064	    /// Returns an error if the request fails or the server returns a non-2xx
  3065	    /// status. This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is
  3066	    /// acceptable.
  3067	    fn post_url(url: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {
  3068	        ureq::post(url)
  3069	            .set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  3070	            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))
  3071	            .send_string(json)
  3072	            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("webhook POST to {url} failed: {e}"))?;
  3073	        Ok(())
  3074	    }
  3075	}

  3098	/// Non-blocking telemetry emitter.
  3099	///
  3100	/// Cloning a `Telemetry` handle is cheap — it shares the same background
  3101	/// writer and sequence counter.
  3102	///
  3103	/// The writer task must be started by calling `start()` from within a tokio
  3104	/// runtime context. This is typically done at the beginning of `Worker::run()`.
  3105	#[derive(Clone)]
  3106	pub struct Telemetry {
  3107	    worker_id: WorkerId,
  3108	    session_id: String,
  3109	    sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,
  3110	    /// Workspace of the most recently claimed bead, shared by all telemetry handles.
  3111	    current_workspace: Arc<std::sync::RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>>,
  3112	    /// Wrapped in Arc<Mutex<Option<...>>> so that `shutdown()` can drop the
  3113	    /// sender explicitly (closing the channel) even while clones still exist.
  3114	    sender: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<WriterMessage>>>>,
  3115	    /// Pending writer state that needs to be spawned in an async context.
  3116	    /// This is `Some` until `start()` is called.
  3117	    pending_writer: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<PendingWriter>>>,
  3118	    /// JoinHandle for the background writer thread, set by `start()`.
  3119	    /// Uses std::thread::JoinHandle (not tokio::task::JoinHandle) because the
  3120	    /// writer runs in its own dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime,
  3121	    /// ensuring it can process messages before the main runtime's block_on().
  3122	    writer_handle: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>>>,
  3123	    /// OTLP sink shutdown handle (feature-gated).
  3124	    /// Stored separately so we can call its async shutdown method.
  3125	    otlp_shutdown: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<OtlpShutdown>>>,
  3126	}

  3134	    pub model: Option<String>,

  3136	    pub provider: Option<String>,
  3137	    /// The worker's workspace. OTLP sinks reduce this to its basename before export.
  3138	    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,
  3139	}

  3158	/// Holds an OTLP sink for async shutdown (feature-gated).
  3159	enum OtlpShutdown {
  3160	    #[cfg(feature = "otlp")]
  3161	    Sink(std::sync::Arc<crate::telemetry::OtlpSink>),
  3162	    #[cfg(not(feature = "otlp"))]
  3163	    None,
  3164	}
  3165	
  3166	impl OtlpShutdown {
  3167	    /// Shutdown the OTLP sink gracefully.
  3168	    ///
  3169	    /// This drains all batched exports before returning.
  3170	    #[cfg(feature = "otlp")]
  3171	    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {
  3172	        match self {
  3173	            OtlpShutdown::Sink(sink) => {
  3174	                // We need to extract the OtlpSink from Arc to call shutdown
  3175	                // Try to unwrap the Arc - if there are other references, we'll force_flush instead
  3176	                match std::sync::Arc::try_unwrap(sink) {
  3177	                    Ok(otlp) => otlp.shutdown().await,
  3178	                    Err(_) => {
  3179	                        tracing::warn!("Cannot shutdown OTLP sink: Arc has multiple references");
  3180	                        Ok(())
  3181	                    }
  3182	                }
  3183	            }
  3184	        }
  3185	    }
  3186	
  3187	    /// No-op shutdown when OTLP feature is disabled.
  3188	    #[cfg(not(feature = "otlp"))]
  3189	    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {
  3190	        Ok(())
  3191	    }
  3192	}

  3199	    /// Create a telemetry emitter that writes to a `FileSink`.
  3200	    ///
  3201	    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from
  3202	    /// within a tokio runtime context before emitting events.
  3203	    ///
  3204	    /// Writes `worker.booting` directly to the file before returning, so even
  3205	    /// if the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL log.
  3206	    pub fn new(worker_id: WorkerId) -> Self {
  3207	        let session_id = generate_session_id();
  3208	        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
  3209	
  3210	        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();
  3211	        match FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id) {
  3212	            Ok(s) => {
  3213	                // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.
  3214	                // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.
  3215	                // This ensures we have a trace even if the writer thread fails to start.
  3216	                let version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
  3217	                if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {
  3218	                    // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)
  3219	                    let error_msg = e.to_string();
  3220	                    if error_msg.contains("timed out")
  3221	                        || error_msg.contains("filesystem may be hung")
  3222	                    {
  3223	                        eprintln!(
  3224	                            "NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow"
  3225	                        );
  3226	                        eprintln!("  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.");
  3227	                        eprintln!(
  3228	                            "  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors"
  3229	                        );
  3230	                    }
  3231	                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to write boot event directly to file");
  3232	                }
  3233	                sinks.push(Box::new(s));
  3234	            }
  3235	            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create telemetry file sink"),
  3236	        }
  3237	
  3238	        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
  3239	        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };
  3240	
  3241	        Telemetry {
  3242	            worker_id,
  3243	            session_id,
  3244	            sequence,
  3245	            current_workspace: Self::new_workspace_cell(),
  3246	            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),
  3247	            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),
  3248	            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
  3249	            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
  3250	        }
  3251	    }

  4601	/// This macro provides a convenient way to log structured events with the
  4602	/// telemetry system. It automatically serializes the context to JSON and
  4603	/// emits it through the provided telemetry instance.
  4604	///
  4605	/// # Arguments
  4606	///
  4607	/// * `$telemetry` - The telemetry instance to emit through
  4608	/// * `$level` - Log level: "info", "warn", "error", or "debug"
  4609	/// * `$phase` - Phase identifier (e.g., "dispatch", "claim")
  4610	/// * `$context` - JSON object with context data
  4611	/// * `$bead_id` - Optional bead ID
  4612	///
  4613	/// # Example
  4614	///
  4615	/// ```no_run
  4616	/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;
  4617	/// # use needle::log;
  4618	/// # use needle::types::BeadId;
  4619	/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();
  4620	/// // Basic info log
  4621	/// log!(telemetry, "info", "dispatch", {"status": "started"});
  4622	///
  4623	/// // Log with bead context
  4624	/// let bead_id = BeadId::from("needle-123");
  4625	/// log!(telemetry, "info", "claim", {"attempt": 1}, Some(bead_id));
  4626	///
  4627	/// // Error log with context
  4628	/// log!(telemetry, "error", "outcome", {
  4629	///     "exit_code": 1,
  4630	///     "reason": "timeout"
  4631	/// }, None::<BeadId>);
  4632	/// ```
  4633	#[macro_export]
  4634	macro_rules! log {
  4635	    ($telemetry:expr, $level:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {
  4636	        $telemetry.log(
  4637	            $phase,
  4638	            $level,
  4639	            $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }),
  4640	            None,
  4641	        )
  4642	    };
  4643	    ($telemetry:expr, $level:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {
  4644	        $telemetry.log(
  4645	            $phase,
  4646	            $level,
  4647	            $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }),
  4648	            $bead_id,
  4649	        )
  4650	    };
  4651	}

  1632	/// Create an OpenTelemetry tracing layer for the tracing subscriber.
  1633	///
  1634	/// This bridges `tracing` spans to the OTLP exporter, allowing use of
  1635	/// `#[instrument]` macros throughout the codebase.
  1636	///
  1637	/// Returns `None` if the OTLP feature is not enabled or if the layer
  1638	/// cannot be created.
  1639	///
  1640	/// The `agent`, `model`, and `workspace` parameters are optional resource
  1641	/// attributes for OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
  1642	///
  1643	/// Note: Drop events from the tracing layer are logged at WARN level
  1644	/// rather than emitted to the file sink, because the tracing layer is
  1645	/// created before the file sink is available.
  1646	#[cfg(feature = "otlp")]
  1647	pub fn create_tracing_layer(
  1648	    worker_id: String,
  1649	    session_id: String,
  1650	    config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
  1651	    agent: Option<&str>,
  1652	    model: Option<&str>,
  1653	    workspace: Option<&str>,
  1654	) -> Result<Option<Box<dyn tracing_subscriber::Layer<tracing_subscriber::Registry> + Send + Sync>>>
  1655	{
  1656	    if !config.enabled {
  1657	        return Ok(None);
  1658	    }
  1659	
  1660	    // Build resource attributes from config + computed attributes
  1661	    let resource = OtlpSink::build_resource(
  1662	        &worker_id,
  1663	        &session_id,
  1664	        config,
  1665	        agent,
  1666	        model,
  1667	        None,
  1668	        workspace,
  1669	    )?;
  1670	
  1671	    // Create drop channel for the tracing layer
  1672	    // Dumps will be logged at WARN level rather than emitted as events
  1673	    // Note: Drop handler spawn deferred to avoid runtime initialization issues
  1674	    let (drop_tx, _drop_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<DropEvent>();
  1675	
  1676	    // Build exporters based on protocol
  1677	    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match config.protocol.as_str() {
  1678	        "grpc" => OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
  1679	        "http" | "http/protobuf" => OtlpSink::build_http_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
  1680	        other => anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'"),
  1681	    };
  1682	
  1683	    // Create the tracing layer with the tracer provider, boxed for type erasure
  1684	    let layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer("needle"));
  1685	    Ok(Some(Box::new(layer)))
  1686	}
  1687	
  1688	impl crate::telemetry::Sink for OtlpSink {
  1689	    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {
  1690	        // Wrap dispatch_event in catch_unwind to prevent OTel SDK panics
  1691	        // from bubbling up to the worker loop. Log failures but don't propagate.
  1692	        match catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| self.dispatch_event(event))) {
  1693	            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),
  1694	            Ok(Err(e)) => {
  1695	                // dispatch_event returned an error - log and suppress
  1696	                warn!("OTLP sink dispatch error: {e}");
  1697	                Ok(())
  1698	            }
  1699	            Err(_) => {
  1700	                // OTel SDK panicked - log and suppress
  1701	                warn!("OTLP sink panicked while dispatching event");
  1702	                Ok(())
  1703	            }
  1704	        }
  1705	    }
  1706	
  1707	    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {
  1708	        // Hard 5-second deadline for shutdown flush, per the OTLP resilience spec.
  1709	        // This is a maximum time we're willing to wait for the collector to acknowledge
  1710	        // all pending telemetry. Past this point, we abandon remaining batches and emit
  1711	        // a shutdown_timeout event to the file sink.
  1712	        let hard_deadline = Duration::from_secs(5).min(deadline);
  1713	
  1714	        // Clone Arcs for move into spawned threads
  1715	        let tracer_provider = self.tracer_provider.clone();
  1716	        let meter_provider = self.meter_provider.clone();
  1717	        let logger_provider = self.logger_provider.clone();
  1718	
  1719	        // Spawn threads for each flush with timeout
  1720	        let tracer_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
  1721	            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1722	                tracer_provider.force_flush()
  1723	            }))
  1724	        });
  1725	        let meter_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
  1726	            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1727	                meter_provider.force_flush()
  1728	            }))
  1729	        });
  1730	        let logger_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
  1731	            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1732	                logger_provider.force_flush()
  1733	            }))
  1734	        });
  1735	
  1736	        // Wait for each flush with the hard deadline
  1737	        // Use join_timeout pattern: sleep for deadline, then check if thread is finished
  1738	        let (tracer_result, tracer_timed_out) =
  1739	            self.join_with_timeout(tracer_handle, hard_deadline, "tracer");
  1740	        let (meter_result, meter_timed_out) =
  1741	            self.join_with_timeout(meter_handle, hard_deadline, "meter");
  1742	        let (logger_result, logger_timed_out) =
  1743	            self.join_with_timeout(logger_handle, hard_deadline, "logger");
  1744	
  1745	        // Collect providers that timed out
  1746	        let mut timed_out_providers = Vec::new();
  1747	        if tracer_timed_out {
  1748	            timed_out_providers.push("tracer");
  1749	        }
  1750	        if meter_timed_out {
  1751	            timed_out_providers.push("meter");
  1752	        }
  1753	        if logger_timed_out {
  1754	            timed_out_providers.push("logger");
  1755	        }
  1756	
  1757	        // Emit shutdown_timeout event if any provider timed out
  1758	        if !timed_out_providers.is_empty() {
  1759	            self.emit_shutdown_timeout_event(&timed_out_providers, hard_deadline);
  1760	        }
  1761	
  1762	        // Check if any flush failed (but don't fail if they timed out - we already logged)
  1763	        tracer_result.context("failed to flush tracer provider")?;
  1764	        meter_result.context("failed to flush meter provider")?;
  1765	        logger_result.context("failed to flush logger provider")?;
  1766	
  1767	        Ok(())
  1768	    }
  1769	}
  1770	
  1771	impl OtlpSink {
  1772	    /// Emit a shutdown_timeout event to the file sink.
  1773	    ///
  1774	    /// This event indicates that one or more OTLP providers failed to flush within
  1775	    /// the 5-second shutdown deadline, causing remaining batches to be abandoned.
  1776	    fn emit_shutdown_timeout_event(&self, providers: &[&str], deadline: Duration) {
  1777	        if let Some(sink) = &self.file_sink {
  1778	            let sequence = self.next_drop_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  1779	
  1780	            let mut data = serde_json::map::Map::new();
  1781	            data.insert(
  1782	                "providers".to_string(),
  1783	                serde_json::json!(providers.join(",")),
  1784	            );
  1785	            data.insert(
  1786	                "deadline_secs".to_string(),
  1787	                serde_json::json!(deadline.as_secs_f64()),
  1788	            );
  1789	            data.insert("abandoned_batches".to_string(), serde_json::json!(true));
  1790	
  1791	            let event = TelemetryEvent {
  1792	                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),
  1793	                event_type: "telemetry.otlp.shutdown_timeout".to_string(),
  1794	                worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
  1795	                session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
  1796	                sequence,
  1797	                bead_id: None,
  1798	                workspace: None,
  1799	                duration_ms: None,
  1800	                data: serde_json::Value::Object(data),
  1801	                trace_id: None,
  1802	                span_id: None,
  1803	            };
  1804	
  1805	            // Emit to file sink - ignore errors to avoid recursion
  1806	            let _ = catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1807	                if let Err(e) = (**sink).accept(&event) {
  1808	                    warn!("failed to write OTLP shutdown_timeout event to file sink: {e}");
  1809	                }
  1810	            }));
  1811	        }
  1812	    }
  1813	
  1814	    /// Helper to join a thread with a timeout.
  1815	    ///
  1816	    /// This is a synchronous timeout implementation since we're not in an async context.
  1817	    /// The pattern is: spawn thread, sleep for deadline, check if done.
  1818	    /// If not done, we consider it timed out and return an error.
  1819	    ///
  1820	    /// Returns (result, timed_out) where timed_out is true if the thread did not
  1821	    /// complete within the deadline.
  1822	    fn join_with_timeout(
  1823	        &self,
  1824	        handle: std::thread::JoinHandle<
  1825	            std::prelude::v1::Result<
  1826	                std::prelude::v1::Result<(), opentelemetry_sdk::error::OTelSdkError>,
  1827	                Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>,
  1828	            >,
  1829	        >,
  1830	        timeout: Duration,
  1831	        name: &str,
  1832	    ) -> (anyhow::Result<()>, bool) {
  1833	        // Sleep for the timeout duration
  1834	        std::thread::sleep(timeout);
  1835	
  1835	
  1836	        // Check if the thread is done
  1837	        if handle.is_finished() {
  1838	            // Thread is done, join it (should return immediately)
  1839	            match handle.join() {
  1840	                Ok(Ok(result)) => {
  1841	                    // Convert OTelSdkError to anyhow::Error
  1842	                    (result.map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("{e}")), false)
  1843	                }
  1844	                Ok(Err(e)) => {
  1845	                    warn!("OTLP {name} provider flush failed: {:?}", e);
  1846	                    (Err(anyhow::anyhow!("{name} provider flush failed")), false)
  1847	                }
  1848	                Err(_) => {
  1849	                    warn!("OTLP {name} provider flush panicked");
  1850	                    (Ok(()), false)
  1851	                }
  1852	            }
  1853	        } else {
  1854	            // Thread is still running, consider it timed out
  1855	            warn!("OTLP {name} provider flush timed out after {timeout:?}");
  1856	            (Ok(()), true)
  1857	        }
  1858	    }
  1859	}

docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:1:# ADR-017: Configuration Hot-Reload at the Cycle Boundary
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-2-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-3-**Status:** Proposed — 2026-08-21
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-4-**Deciders:** operator (jedarden)
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-5-**Tracking:** plan.md §18; motivated by the 2026-08-21 fleet-wide OTLP migration
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-6-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-7-## Context
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-8-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-9-On 2026-08-21 the ex44 fleet was migrated to OTLP export. The change that had
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-10-to take effect was a single boolean — `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled` in
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-11-`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`. Applying it required draining and relaunching
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-12-**all fifteen workers**, a rollover that took ~55 minutes of wall clock and was
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-13-bounded not by the work but by however long each worker's in-flight agent
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-14-dispatch happened to run. Every drained worker released its in-flight bead.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-15-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-16-Nothing in NEEDLE can pick up a configuration change in place. `Config` says so
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-17-in its own doc comment — "Loaded once at boot, immutable during a session" — and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-18-the runtime is built to match:
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-19-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-20-- `Worker::new` constructs `Telemetry::from_config`, `StrandRunner::from_config`,
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-21-  `PromptBuilder::new`, `Dispatcher::new`, `OutcomeHandler::new`,
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-22-  `HealthMonitor::new`, and `RateLimiter::new` **once**, each from a snapshot of
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-23-  the config, and holds them for the process lifetime.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-24-- `init_tracing_subscriber` (`cli/mod.rs`) installs the OTLP tracing layer with
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-25-  `tracing_subscriber::registry()....try_init()` — a **process-global, one-shot**
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-26-  install. There is no second chance at it, by design of the tracing crate.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-27-- The remaining config lives in `self.config: Config`, an owned copy read live on
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-28-  many paths (`worker.idle_action`, `worker.max_claim_retries`, `agent.default`,
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-29-  `workspace.default`, …). These would already follow a swapped value.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-30-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-31-Three properties of the 2026-08-21 incident are what this ADR is actually
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-32-responding to:
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-33-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-34-1. **The cost of a config change is a fleet rollover.** Not a restart of one
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-35-   process — a staged drain of every worker, each releasing a claimed bead.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-36-2. **A config flip is *armed*, not inert.** needle ≥0.4 fails closed when
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-37-   `otlp_sink.enabled` is true and `NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION` is absent:
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-38-   `init_tracing_subscriber` → `build_http_providers()?` propagates and the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:39:   worker refuses to boot. Editing the file while a header-less fleet runs does
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-40-   not do nothing — it means the *next* restart of each worker kills it.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-41-3. **Config that cannot apply is silently discarded.** `telemetry` sits in
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-42-   `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS`, so `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` in a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-43-   workspace `.needle.yaml` is parsed, warned to a log nobody reads, and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-44-   dropped. The fleet ran for days with a config file that looked correct.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-45-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-46-The seam this needs already exists: `check_hot_reload()` runs after the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-47-`LOGGING` state, described in-code as running "between dispatch cycles, never
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-48-mid-claim, ensuring no bead is left in_progress." Configuration reload is the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-49-same problem with a smaller blast radius.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-50-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-51-**But that seam's own history is a warning, not a reassurance.**
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-52-`check_hot_reload` carried `#[allow(dead_code)]` and had **no call site
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-53-anywhere** from its introduction on 2026-03-21 until it was wired in around
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-54-2026-08-16 (`needle-eea03800`) — for five months, while its doc comment stated
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-55-it was "called between LOGGING and SELECTING." Every deploy in that window was
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-56-a manual kill-and-relaunch that people believed was a hot-reload. It is
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-57-genuinely live now (21 `binary.freshness.exit` events as of 2026-08-21), so the
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-58-boundary is real and exercised — but it has days of production evidence, not
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-59-months.
--
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-101-The tier is declared in code as a table, not inferred:
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-102-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-103-| Tier | Meaning | Examples |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-104-|---|---|---|
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-105-| **A — live** | Swap `self.config`; effective next cycle, no rebuild. | `worker.idle_*`, `worker.max_claim_retries`, `agent.timeout`, `budget.*`, strand thresholds |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-106-| **B — rebuild** | Component reconstructed from the new config at the boundary. | `telemetry.*` sinks, `strands.*`, `prompt.*`, `agent.adapters_dir`, `limits.*`, gates/verification |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-107-| **C — immutable** | Requires a restart. | worker identity / `qualified_id`, `workspace.home`, `bead_cli.backend`, the tokio runtime, the shape of the tracing subscriber stack |
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-108-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-109-**Rejected:** a single atomic swap of the whole `Config` with no tiering. It
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-110-reads as if everything is reloadable, and would silently no-op for the Tier-C
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-111-keys — recreating the exact `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` failure that caused this
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-112-work.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-113-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-114-### 4. Validate before swap; a reload may never fail closed
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-115-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-116-The candidate config is validated with the existing `ConfigLoader::validate`
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-117-before anything is swapped. On any error the running config is kept, a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-118-`config.reload.rejected` event is emitted with the errors, and the worker
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-119-continues on its current configuration.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-120-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:121:This is non-negotiable and is the direct lesson of the OTLP header: a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-122-configuration problem must degrade telemetry, never remove a worker. A typo in a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-123-YAML file must not be able to take down the fleet — and with polled reload, a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-124-bad edit would otherwise reach every worker simultaneously within one interval,
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-125-which is *worse* than the restart-only status quo.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-126-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-127-### 5. The reload seam is installed unconditionally at boot
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-128-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-129-The OTLP tracing layer is wrapped in `tracing_subscriber::reload::Layer` from
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-130-the first moment of process start — **including when OTLP is disabled**, where
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-131-it wraps a no-op layer.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-132-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-133-This is the load-bearing decision. `try_init()` is one-shot: a process that
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-134-booted without a reload handle can never acquire one. If the seam is installed
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-135-only when OTLP is already enabled, then turning OTLP *on* still requires a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-136-restart — which is precisely the situation this ADR exists to eliminate, and it
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-137-would not be discovered until someone tried it on a live fleet. `reload` is not
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-138-feature-gated in the pinned `tracing-subscriber` 0.3.23, so this costs no new
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-139-dependency.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-140-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-141-### 6. Changes that cannot be applied are reported, never silently ignored
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-142-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:143:A Tier-C key changing produces a `config.reload.restart_required` event naming
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-144-the keys, and a WARN. The same applies to a workspace `.needle.yaml` carrying a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-145-`NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` section. Silence is what let the fleet run for days on a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-146-config file that read as correct.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-147-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-148-### 7. Secrets are re-resolved, never re-logged, and never tear down a live exporter
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-149-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:150:`env:`-prefixed header values are re-resolved from the process environment on a
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:151:Tier-B telemetry rebuild. A reload **cannot** introduce a new environment
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:152:variable into a running process, so if a rebuild would need a header the process
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-153-does not have, the existing exporter is kept and the condition reported. A
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-154-reload must never convert a working exporter into a dead one. Header values are
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-155-never written to a log, an event, or an error message.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-156-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-157-## Consequences
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-158-
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-159-- Enabling or disabling OTLP, changing timeouts, thresholds, gates, or prompts
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-160-  becomes a file edit plus at most one check interval — no drain, no released
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-161-  beads, no rollover.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-162-- A restart remains required for identity, `workspace.home`, bead backend, and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-163-  runtime-shaped concerns. That set is now explicit rather than discovered.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md:164:- Tier-B rebuilds add bounded latency at the cycle boundary. Mitigated by
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-165-  hashing per config section and rebuilding only components whose own subtree
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-166-  changed.
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-167-- The blast radius of a bad config edit grows from "the next worker to restart"
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-168-  to "every worker within one interval". Decision 4 is what makes that safe, and
docs/adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md-169-  is the reason validation is a hard gate rather than a warning.

docs/plan/plan.md-1987-Design:
docs/plan/plan.md-1988-
docs/plan/plan.md-1989-- **Non-blocking.** Uses a batch span/log/metric processor. If the collector is unreachable, events are buffered up to a bounded queue, then dropped (same policy as file sink). Drops emit a `telemetry.otlp.dropped` event to the file sink (never recursively to OTLP).
docs/plan/plan.md-1990-- **Additive.** The file sink is authoritative. OTLP is an export, not a replacement. If OTLP is disabled or misconfigured, NEEDLE behaves identically to a file-sink-only deployment.
docs/plan/plan.md-1991-- **Stdlib deps.** Rust crates: `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions`. All support OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP.

docs/plan/plan.md-3392-
docs/plan/plan.md-3393-**Rule source: gitleaks.** Rather than hand-rolling regex patterns, NEEDLE imports the rule database from [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks) — the industry-standard secret detection tool. Gitleaks ships 222 rules in a single TOML file (`config/gitleaks.toml`) covering 120+ services across cloud providers, AI/ML platforms, CI/CD, payment processors, communication tools, and generic patterns. The regexes use RE2 syntax, which is directly compatible with Rust's `regex` crate.
docs/plan/plan.md-3394-
docs/plan/plan.md-3395-**Sanitization pipeline (applied to all trace content before write):**
docs/plan/plan.md-3396-
docs/plan/plan.md-3397-1. **Gitleaks rule set.** NEEDLE vendors a copy of `gitleaks.toml` at build time and parses the `[[rules]]` entries. Each rule provides:
docs/plan/plan.md-3398-   - `regex` — RE2 pattern matching the secret
docs/plan/plan.md-3399-   - `keywords` — fast pre-filter strings checked before the expensive regex (Aho-Corasick). If keywords are specified and none are found in the content, the regex is skipped.
docs/plan/plan.md-3400-   - `secretGroup` — which capture group contains the actual secret (only that portion is redacted, preserving surrounding context)
docs/plan/plan.md-3401-   - `entropy` — minimum Shannon entropy threshold. Distinguishes real secrets from placeholders like `your-api-key-here`.
docs/plan/plan.md-3402-
docs/plan/plan.md-3403-   Key rule categories:
docs/plan/plan.md-3404-   | Category | Examples | Rule Count |
docs/plan/plan.md-3405-   |----------|----------|------------|
docs/plan/plan.md-3406-   | Cloud providers | AWS access keys, Azure AD secrets, GCP API keys | ~25 |
docs/plan/plan.md-3407-   | AI/ML | Anthropic, OpenAI, HuggingFace, Cohere API keys | ~8 |
docs/plan/plan.md-3408-   | Git/CI/CD | GitHub PATs, GitLab tokens, CircleCI, Drone | ~25 |
docs/plan/plan.md-3409-   | Communication | Slack (8 token types), Discord, Telegram, Twilio | ~15 |
docs/plan/plan.md-3410-   | Payment/Finance | Stripe, Plaid, Coinbase, Kraken | ~12 |
docs/plan/plan.md-3411-   | DevOps/Infra | HashiCorp Vault, Grafana, Datadog, Sentry | ~15 |
docs/plan/plan.md:3412:   | Generic | `generic-api-key`, JWT, private keys (RSA/EC), curl auth headers | ~10 |
docs/plan/plan.md-3413-   | Package registries | npm, PyPI, NuGet, RubyGems | ~8 |
docs/plan/plan.md-3414-
docs/plan/plan.md-3415-   Redaction output includes the rule ID for auditability: `[REDACTED:aws-access-token]`
docs/plan/plan.md-3416-
docs/plan/plan.md-3417-2. **Custom patterns.** Workspace-specific patterns configured in `.needle.yaml`, applied after the gitleaks rules:
docs/plan/plan.md-3418-   ```yaml
docs/plan/plan.md-3419-   learning:
docs/plan/plan.md-3420-     trace_sanitization:
docs/plan/plan.md-3421-       custom_patterns:
docs/plan/plan.md-3422-         - id: "kalshi-api-key"
docs/plan/plan.md-3423-           regex: "KALSHI_API_KEY=[^\\s]+"
docs/plan/plan.md-3424-           keywords: ["kalshi"]
docs/plan/plan.md-3425-         - id: "openbao-token"
docs/plan/plan.md-3426-           regex: "openbao\\s+token\\s+\\S+"
docs/plan/plan.md-3427-           keywords: ["openbao"]
docs/plan/plan.md-3428-       redaction_text: "[REDACTED]"    # default: "[REDACTED:<rule-id>]"
docs/plan/plan.md-3429-   ```
docs/plan/plan.md-3430-
docs/plan/plan.md-3431-3. **Gitleaks allowlists and stopwords.** The gitleaks rule set includes per-rule allowlists (regexes, paths, stopwords) and ~1,480 global stopwords that suppress common false positives (e.g., `example`, `test`, `placeholder`). NEEDLE applies these to reduce over-redaction.
