docs/plan/plan.md-4693-
docs/plan/plan.md-4694-# Phase 18: Configuration Hot-Reload at the Cycle Boundary
docs/plan/plan.md-4695-
docs/plan/plan.md:4696:**Status:** proposed (ADR-017).
docs/plan/plan.md-4697-
docs/plan/plan.md:4698:**Goal:** make a configuration change take effect on a running worker without a restart, at the boundary where it is already safe to change things. Driven by the 2026-08-21 fleet-wide OTLP migration: flipping one boolean (`telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled`) required draining and relaunching all fifteen ex44 workers — ~55 minutes of wall clock, bounded by whatever each worker's in-flight dispatch happened to be doing, with every drained worker releasing its claimed bead. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-017](../adr/017-configuration-hot-reload-at-the-cycle-boundary.md).
docs/plan/plan.md-4699-
docs/plan/plan.md-4700-The runtime is built to make this impossible today, in three distinct ways:
docs/plan/plan.md-4701-
docs/plan/plan.md-4702-1. **Config is a boot-time snapshot.** `Config`'s own doc comment says "Loaded once at boot, immutable during a session." `Worker::new` builds `Telemetry`, `StrandRunner`, `PromptBuilder`, `Dispatcher`, `OutcomeHandler`, `HealthMonitor`, and `RateLimiter` from that snapshot and holds them for the process lifetime.
docs/plan/plan.md-4703-2. **The tracing subscriber is a one-shot global.** `init_tracing_subscriber` installs the OTLP layer via `tracing_subscriber::registry()....try_init()`. A process that booted without a reload handle can never acquire one.
docs/plan/plan.md-4704-3. **Unapplicable config is discarded silently.** `telemetry` is in `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS`, so a workspace `.needle.yaml` enabling OTLP is parsed, warned once, and dropped. The fleet ran for days on a config file that read as correct.
docs/plan/plan.md-4705-
docs/plan/plan.md-4706-The safe seam already exists: `check_hot_reload()` runs after `LOGGING`, "between dispatch cycles, never mid-claim, ensuring no bead is left in_progress." Config reload is the same problem with a smaller blast radius.
docs/plan/plan.md-4707-
docs/plan/plan.md-4708-**That seam's history is itself a requirement.** `check_hot_reload` was `#[allow(dead_code)]` with no call site anywhere from 2026-03-21 until ~2026-08-16 (`needle-eea03800`) — five months during which its doc comment claimed it ran between LOGGING and SELECTING, and every "hot-reload" deploy was really a manual kill-and-relaunch. It is live now (21 `binary.freshness.exit` events as of 2026-08-21), but that is days of evidence, not months. A reload mechanism that is *documented* to run is not one that runs: Phase 18 must assert the config check actually executes, and fail if the call site is ever dropped.
docs/plan/plan.md-4709-
docs/plan/plan.md-4710-## Decisions locked
docs/plan/plan.md-4711-
docs/plan/plan.md-4712-An implementer will hit each of these forks; the plan decides them so no mid-build ADR is needed.
docs/plan/plan.md-4713-
docs/plan/plan.md-4714-- **Trigger = polled mtime+hash at the cycle boundary**, gated by `worker.config_reload_check_interval_secs` (`0` = disabled, and is the default until the feature has fleet time). *Because* it mirrors `check_hot_reload`'s existing binary-hash check and adds no dependency. *Rejected:* a `notify` file watcher (new dep, new async task, and it must defer to the boundary anyway). *Enforced by* 18.2.
docs/plan/plan.md-4715-- **SIGHUP must NOT be the trigger.** *Because* `install_unix_signal_handlers` already registers `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`/`SIGHUP` onto the shutdown flag, deliberately — a killed tmux session delivers SIGHUP, and the handler exists so the worker can release its bead and emit `worker.stopped` rather than die silently. Repurposing it turns every tmux teardown into a reload. *Revisit if* the shutdown handler ever stops covering SIGHUP.
docs/plan/plan.md-4716-- **Reload applies only between dispatch cycles.** *Because* a worker in `Building`/`Dispatching`/`Executing`/`Handling` holds a bead, and changing `agent.timeout` or an adapter under a running dispatch produces an outcome attributable to neither config. *Enforced by* 18.2 + the test in 18.8.
docs/plan/plan.md-4717-- **Three declared tiers, written as a table in code, not inferred.** *Because* an untiered atomic swap reads as though everything is reloadable and would silently no-op for immutable keys — recreating the `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` failure that caused this work. *Enforced by* 18.1.
docs/plan/plan.md-4718-- **Validate before swap; a reload may never fail closed.** *Because* polled reload reaches every worker within one interval, so a bad edit is fleet-wide and simultaneous — strictly worse than the restart-only status quo unless validation is a hard gate. A config problem must degrade telemetry, never remove a worker. *Enforced by* 18.3.
docs/plan/plan.md:4719:- **The `reload::Layer` seam is installed unconditionally at boot, including when OTLP is off.** *Because* `try_init()` is one-shot; installing the seam only when OTLP is already enabled means turning OTLP *on* still needs a restart — the exact situation this phase exists to remove, undiscoverable until tried on a live fleet. *Enforced by* 18.5.
docs/plan/plan.md:4720:- **A reload never tears down a working exporter.** *Because* a reload cannot introduce a new environment variable into a running process, so a rebuild needing an absent `env:` header must keep the old exporter and report. *Enforced by* 18.5.
docs/plan/plan.md-4721-
docs/plan/plan.md-4722-## Changes
docs/plan/plan.md-4723-
docs/plan/plan.md-4724-### 18.1 Declare a reload tier for every config key
docs/plan/plan.md:4725:- A table in `src/config/` mapping each key path to **Tier A (live)**, **Tier B (rebuild)**, or **Tier C (restart-required)**.
docs/plan/plan.md-4726-- Tier A: `worker.idle_*`, `worker.max_claim_retries`, `agent.timeout`, `budget.*`, strand thresholds — read live off `self.config`, effective next cycle with no rebuild.
docs/plan/plan.md:4727:- Tier B: `telemetry.*`, `strands.*`, `prompt.*`, `agent.adapters_dir`, `limits.*`, gates/verification — owned by a component built in `Worker::new`.
docs/plan/plan.md-4728-- Tier C: worker identity/`qualified_id`, `workspace.home`, `bead_cli.backend`, tokio runtime, tracing-stack shape.
docs/plan/plan.md-4729-- **Normative rule:** a new config key must be assigned a tier in the same change that introduces it. An unclassified key is a compile-time failure, not a runtime surprise.
docs/plan/plan.md-4730-
docs/plan/plan.md-4731-### 18.2 Cycle-boundary reload check
docs/plan/plan.md-4732-- `check_config_reload()` alongside `check_hot_reload()` after `do_log()`, gated by `worker.config_reload_check_interval_secs`.
docs/plan/plan.md-4733-- Detect via mtime plus content hash of the resolved global config path (mtime alone is not sufficient — an editor that rewrites in place with a preserved mtime would be missed).
docs/plan/plan.md-4734-- Per-section hashing so 18.4 can rebuild only the components whose own subtree changed.
docs/plan/plan.md-4735-
docs/plan/plan.md-4736-### 18.3 Validate-before-swap, and never fail closed
docs/plan/plan.md-4737-- Run `ConfigLoader::validate` against the candidate before any swap.
docs/plan/plan.md-4738-- On error: keep the running config, emit `config.reload.rejected` with the errors, WARN, continue. Never propagate a reload error into the worker's `Result` path — that is how a config problem becomes a dead worker.
docs/plan/plan.md-4739-- The swap itself is all-or-nothing: no half-applied configuration is ever observable.
docs/plan/plan.md-4740-
docs/plan/plan.md:4741:### 18.4 Rebuild Tier-B components
docs/plan/plan.md-4742-- Reconstruct only components whose config subtree changed: `StrandRunner`, `PromptBuilder`, `Dispatcher` (adapter reload), `RateLimiter`, `OutcomeHandler`.
docs/plan/plan.md-4743-- Each rebuild is fallible and isolated: a component that fails to rebuild keeps its previous instance and reports, rather than leaving the worker with a missing component.
docs/plan/plan.md-4744-
docs/plan/plan.md:4745:### 18.5 Reload-safe telemetry
docs/plan/plan.md-4746-- Wrap the OTLP tracing layer in `tracing_subscriber::reload::Layer` at boot **unconditionally**, wrapping a no-op layer when OTLP is disabled. `reload` is not feature-gated in the pinned `tracing-subscriber` 0.3.23 — no new dependency.
docs/plan/plan.md-4747-- Make the telemetry writer thread's sink set swappable. The thread currently owns `Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>` for its lifetime (`PendingWriter`); add a control message on the existing channel so sinks can be replaced without tearing down the writer or losing queued events.
docs/plan/plan.md:4748:- Re-resolve `env:`-prefixed header values from the process environment on rebuild. If a required header is absent, keep the existing exporter and emit `config.reload.restart_required` — never replace a working exporter with a dead one. Header values never reach a log, event, or error message.
docs/plan/plan.md-4749-
docs/plan/plan.md-4750-### 18.6 Report what cannot be applied
docs/plan/plan.md:4751:- A Tier-C key change emits `config.reload.restart_required` naming the keys, plus a WARN.
docs/plan/plan.md-4752-- The same treatment for a workspace `.needle.yaml` carrying a `NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS` section — currently a single WARN into a log nobody reads.
docs/plan/plan.md-4753-
docs/plan/plan.md-4754-### 18.7 Observability
docs/plan/plan.md:4755:- Events: `config.reload.detected`, `config.reload.applied` (with the changed key paths), `config.reload.rejected`, `config.reload.restart_required`.
docs/plan/plan.md-4756-- `needle config --dump --show-source` must reflect the **live** config of a running worker, including a reload generation counter, so an operator can confirm what a worker is actually running rather than what the file says.

   690	    /// Background task that monitors for export failures and emits drop events.
   691	    ///
   692	    /// This task runs for the lifetime of the OtlpSink, receiving drop notifications
   693	    /// from exporter wrappers and emitting `telemetry.otlp.dropped` events to the
   694	    /// file sink only (never to OTLP, to avoid recursion).
   695	    #[allow(dead_code)] // Used in tests only
   696	    async fn drop_monitor_task(
   697	        mut drop_rx: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<DropEvent>,
   698	        file_sink: Option<Arc<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>>,
   699	        worker_id: String,
   700	        session_id: String,
   701	        next_drop_sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   702	    ) {
   703	        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {
   704	            if let Some(sink) = &file_sink {
   705	                let sequence = next_drop_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
   706	
   707	                let mut data = serde_json::map::Map::new();
   708	                data.insert(
   709	                    "signal".to_string(),
   710	                    serde_json::json!(drop.signal.as_str()),
   711	                );
   712	                data.insert(
   713	                    "dropped_count".to_string(),
   714	                    serde_json::json!(drop.dropped_count),
   715	                );
   716	                data.insert("queue_full".to_string(), serde_json::json!(true));
   717	
   718	                let event = TelemetryEvent {
   719	                    timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),
   720	                    event_type: "telemetry.otlp.dropped".to_string(),
   721	                    worker_id: worker_id.clone(),
   722	                    session_id: session_id.clone(),
   723	                    sequence,
   724	                    bead_id: None,
   725	                    workspace: None,
   726	                    duration_ms: None,
   727	                    data: serde_json::Value::Object(data),
   728	                    trace_id: None,
   729	                    span_id: None,
   730	                };
   731	
   732	                // Emit to file sink - ignore errors to avoid recursion
   733	                let _ = catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
   734	                    if let Err(e) = (**sink).accept(&event) {
   735	                        warn!("failed to write OTLP drop event to file sink: {e}");
   736	                    }
   737	                }));
   738	            }
   739	        }
   740	    }

   878	    where

   892	    fn build_grpc_providers_with_exporters_inner<S, L>(
   893	        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
   894	        resource: &Resource,
   895	        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,
   896	        metadata: tonic::metadata::MetadataMap,
   897	        base_span_exporter: S,
   898	        base_log_exporter: L,
   899	    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>
   900	    where
   901	        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,
   902	        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,
   903	    {
   904	        use opentelemetry_otlp::{MetricExporter, WithExportConfig, WithTonicConfig};
   905	
   906	        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);
   907	
   908	        let span_exporter = ResilientGrpcSpanExporter::new(base_span_exporter, drop_tx.clone());
   909	        let batch_span_processor = BatchSpanProcessor::builder(span_exporter).build();
   910	        let tracer_provider = SdkTracerProvider::builder()
   911	            .with_span_processor(batch_span_processor)
   912	            .with_resource(resource.clone())
   913	            .build();
   914	
   915	        let metric_exporter = MetricExporter::builder()
   916	            .with_tonic()
   917	            .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone())
   918	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   919	            .with_metadata(metadata.clone())
   920	            .build()?;
   921	        let metric_reader = PeriodicReader::builder(metric_exporter)
   922	            .with_interval(Duration::from_secs(config.metrics_interval_secs))
   923	            .build();
   924	        let meter_provider = SdkMeterProvider::builder()
   925	            .with_reader(metric_reader)
   926	            .with_resource(resource.clone())
   927	            .build();
   928	
   929	        let log_exporter = ResilientGrpcLogExporter::new(base_log_exporter, drop_tx);
   930	        let batch_log_processor = BatchLogProcessor::builder(log_exporter).build();
   931	        let logger_provider = SdkLoggerProvider::builder()
   932	            .with_log_processor(batch_log_processor)
   933	            .with_resource(resource.clone())
   934	            .build();
   935	
   936	        Ok((tracer_provider, meter_provider, logger_provider))
   937	    }

   939	    fn build_grpc_metadata(config: &OtlpSinkConfig) -> Result<tonic::metadata::MetadataMap> {
   940	        use tonic::metadata::{MetadataKey, MetadataMap, MetadataValue};
   941	
   942	        let mut metadata = MetadataMap::new();
   943	        for (key, value) in resolve_headers(&config.headers)? {
   944	            let key_val = MetadataKey::from_bytes(key.as_bytes())
   945	                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid OTLP metadata header name '{key}'"))?;
   946	            let metadata_value = MetadataValue::try_from(value.as_str())
   947	                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid value for OTLP metadata header '{key}'"))?;
   948	            metadata.insert(key_val, metadata_value);
   949	        }
   950	        Ok(metadata)
   951	    }

   967	        // (/v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs) when the endpoint is resolved from
   968	        // an OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT env var. When `.with_endpoint()` is

   971	        // HTTP export request hits the collector's bare root and gets a 404.

   973	        // None), url: ".../4318/" }, and NEEDLE's own OTLP telemetry has never
   974	        // once reached the dashboard as a result.
   975	        let http_signal_endpoint =
   976	            |path: &str| format!("{}{}", config.endpoint.trim_end_matches('/'), path);
   977

   979	        // transport-seam tests below.
   980	        let base_span_exporter = SpanExporter::builder()
   981	            .with_http()
   982	            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint("/v1/traces"))
   983	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   984	            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())
   985	            .build()?;
   986	        let base_log_exporter = LogExporter::builder()
   987	            .with_http()
   988	            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint("/v1/logs"))
   989	            .with_timeout(timeout)
   990	            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())
   991	            .build()?;
   992	
   993	        Self::build_http_providers_with_exporters_inner(
   994	            config,
   995	            resource,
   996	            drop_tx,
   997	            headers_map,
   998	            base_span_exporter,
   999	            base_log_exporter,
  1000	        )
  1001	    }

  1087	    /// - Spans: bead.claim.attempted, bead.claim.succeeded, bead.claim.race_lost,

  1093	    ///   consumers that do not query the trace backend
  1094	    fn dispatch_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {

  1098	        // joining three signal stores.

  1100

  1102	            // Metrics: worker lifecycle
  1103	            "worker.started" => {
  1104	                self.metrics.workers_active.add(1, &[]);
  1105	            }
  1106	
  1107	            "worker.stopped" => {
  1108	                self.metrics.workers_active.add(-1, &[]);
  1109	            }
  1110	
  1111	            // Events whose analytical representation is a span.
  1112	            "bead.claim.attempted" => {
  1113	                // Track claim attempts with result="attempting"
  1114	                self.metrics
  1115	                    .claim_attempts

  1632	/// Create an OpenTelemetry tracing layer for the tracing subscriber.
  1633	///
  1634	/// This bridges `tracing` spans to the OTLP exporter, allowing use of
  1635	/// `#[instrument]` macros throughout the codebase.
  1636	///
  1637	/// Returns `None` if the OTLP feature is not enabled or if the layer
  1638	/// cannot be created.
  1639	///
  1640	/// The `agent`, `model`, and `workspace` parameters are optional resource
  1641	/// attributes for OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
  1642	///
  1643	/// Note: Drop events from the tracing layer are logged at WARN level
  1644	/// rather than emitted to the file sink, because the tracing layer is
  1645	/// created before the file sink is available.
  1646	#[cfg(feature = "otlp")]
  1647	pub fn create_tracing_layer(
  1648	    worker_id: String,
  1649	    session_id: String,
  1650	    config: &OtlpSinkConfig,
  1651	    agent: Option<&str>,
  1652	    model: Option<&str>,
  1653	    workspace: Option<&str>,
  1654	) -> Result<Option<Box<dyn tracing_subscriber::Layer<tracing_subscriber::Registry> + Send + Sync>>>
  1655	{
  1656	    if !config.enabled {
  1657	        return Ok(None);
  1658	    }
  1659	
  1660	    // Build resource attributes from config + computed attributes
  1661	    let resource = OtlpSink::build_resource(
  1662	        &worker_id,
  1663	        &session_id,
  1664	        config,
  1665	        agent,
  1666	        model,
  1667	        None,
  1668	        workspace,
  1669	    )?;
  1670	
  1671	    // Create drop channel for the tracing layer
  1672	    // Dumps will be logged at WARN level rather than emitted as events
  1673	    // Note: Drop handler spawn deferred to avoid runtime initialization issues
  1674	    let (drop_tx, _drop_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<DropEvent>();
  1675	
  1676	    // Build exporters based on protocol
  1677	    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match config.protocol.as_str() {
  1678	        "grpc" => OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
  1679	        "http" | "http/protobuf" => OtlpSink::build_http_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,
  1680	        other => anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'"),
  1681	    };
  1682	
  1683	    // Create the tracing layer with the tracer provider, boxed for type erasure
  1684	    let layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer("needle"));
  1685	    Ok(Some(Box::new(layer)))
  1686	}

  1688	impl crate::telemetry::Sink for OtlpSink {
  1689	    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {
  1690	        // Wrap dispatch_event in catch_unwind to prevent OTel SDK panics
  1691	        // from bubbling up to the worker loop. Log failures but don't propagate.
  1692	        match catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| self.dispatch_event(event))) {
  1693	            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),
  1694	            Ok(Err(e)) => {
  1695	                // dispatch_event returned an error - log and suppress
  1696	                warn!("OTLP sink dispatch error: {e}");
  1697	                Ok(())
  1698	            }
  1699	            Err(_) => {
  1700	                // OTel SDK panicked - log and suppress
  1701	                warn!("OTLP sink panicked while dispatching event");
  1702	                Ok(())
  1703	            }
  1704	        }
  1705	    }
  1706	
  1707	    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {
  1708	        // Hard 5-second deadline for shutdown flush, per the OTLP resilience spec.
  1709	        // This is a maximum time we're willing to wait for the collector to acknowledge
  1710	        // all pending telemetry. Past this point, we abandon remaining batches and emit
  1711	        // a shutdown_timeout event to the file sink.
  1712	        let hard_deadline = Duration::from_secs(5).min(deadline);
  1713	
  1714	        // Clone Arcs for move into spawned threads
  1715	        let tracer_provider = self.tracer_provider.clone();
  1716	        let meter_provider = self.meter_provider.clone();
  1717	        let logger_provider = self.logger_provider.clone();
  1718	
  1719	        // Spawn threads for each flush with timeout
  1720	        let tracer_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
  1721	            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1722	                tracer_provider.force_flush()
  1723	            }))
  1724	        });
  1725	        let meter_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
  1726	            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1727	                meter_provider.force_flush()
  1728	            }))
  1729	        });
  1730	        let logger_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
  1731	            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1732	                logger_provider.force_flush()
  1733	            }))
  1734	        });
  1735	
  1736	        // Wait for each flush with the hard deadline
  1737	        // Use join_timeout pattern: sleep for deadline, then check if thread is finished
  1738	        let (tracer_result, tracer_timed_out) =
  1739	            self.join_with_timeout(tracer_handle, hard_deadline, "tracer");
  1740	        let (meter_result, meter_timed_out) =
  1741	            self.join_with_timeout(meter_handle, hard_deadline, "meter");
  1742	        let (logger_result, logger_timed_out) =
  1743	            self.join_with_timeout(logger_handle, hard_deadline, "logger");
  1744	
  1745	        // Collect providers that timed out
  1746	        let mut timed_out_providers = Vec::new();
  1747	        if tracer_timed_out {
  1748	            timed_out_providers.push("tracer");
  1749	        }
  1750	        if meter_timed_out {
  1751	            timed_out_providers.push("meter");
  1752	        }
  1753	        if logger_timed_out {
  1754	            timed_out_providers.push("logger");
  1755	        }
  1756	
  1757	        // Emit shutdown_timeout event if any provider timed out
  1758	        if !timed_out_providers.is_empty() {
  1759	            self.emit_shutdown_timeout_event(&timed_out_providers, hard_deadline);
  1760	        }
  1761	
  1762	        // Check if any flush failed (but don't fail if they timed out - we already logged)
  1763	        tracer_result.context("failed to flush tracer provider")?;
  1764	        meter_result.context("failed to flush meter provider")?;
  1765	        logger_result.context("failed to flush logger provider")?;
  1766	
  1767	        Ok(())
  1768	    }
  1769	}
  1770	
  1771	impl OtlpSink {
  1772	    /// Emit a shutdown_timeout event to the file sink.
  1773	    ///
  1774	    /// This event indicates that one or more OTLP providers failed to flush within
  1775	    /// the 5-second shutdown deadline, causing remaining batches to be abandoned.
  1776	    fn emit_shutdown_timeout_event(&self, providers: &[&str], deadline: Duration) {
  1777	        if let Some(sink) = &self.file_sink {
  1778	            let sequence = self.next_drop_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  1779	
  1780	            let mut data = serde_json::map::Map::new();
  1781	            data.insert(
  1782	                "providers".to_string(),
  1783	                serde_json::json!(providers.join(",")),
  1784	            );
  1785	            data.insert(
  1786	                "deadline_secs".to_string(),
  1787	                serde_json::json!(deadline.as_secs_f64()),
  1788	            );
  1789	            data.insert("abandoned_batches".to_string(), serde_json::json!(true));
  1790	
  1791	            let event = TelemetryEvent {
  1792	                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),
  1793	                event_type: "telemetry.otlp.shutdown_timeout".to_string(),
  1794	                worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
  1795	                session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
  1796	                sequence,
  1797	                bead_id: None,
  1798	                workspace: None,
  1799	                duration_ms: None,
  1800	                data: serde_json::Value::Object(data),
  1801	                trace_id: None,
  1802	                span_id: None,
  1803	            };
  1804	
  1805	            // Emit to file sink - ignore errors to avoid recursion
  1806	            let _ = catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  1807	                if let Err(e) = (**sink).accept(&event) {
  1808	                    warn!("failed to write OTLP shutdown_timeout event to file sink: {e}");
  1809	                }
  1810	            }));
  1811	        }
  1812	    }

  3372	    /// Create a telemetry emitter from a `TelemetryConfig`.
  3373	    ///
  3374	    /// Selects the right constructor based on configured sinks:
  3375	    /// - OTLP enabled       → creates OTLP sink with async shutdown
  3376	    /// - Hooks configured   → [`with_hooks`](Self::with_hooks)
  3377	    /// - Stdout enabled     → [`with_stdout`](Self::with_stdout)
  3378	    /// - Otherwise          → [`new`](Self::new) (file sink only)
  3379	    pub fn from_config(worker_id: WorkerId, config: &TelemetryConfig) -> Result<Self> {
  3380	        Self::from_config_with_identity(worker_id, config, &TelemetryIdentity::default())
  3381	    }

  3383	    /// Create a telemetry emitter from configuration with worker identity metadata.
  3384	    ///
  3385	    /// This is the construction path used by a running worker. Keeping the
  3386	    /// identity separate from `TelemetryConfig` avoids putting runtime-resolved
  3387	    /// adapter details into persisted configuration while ensuring every OTLP
  3388	    /// signal receives the same worker metadata.
  3389	    pub fn from_config_with_identity(
  3390	        worker_id: WorkerId,
  3391	        config: &TelemetryConfig,
  3392	        identity: &TelemetryIdentity,
  3393	    ) -> Result<Self> {

  3398	        let mut otlp_shutdown = None;
  3399	        let mut file_sink: Option<Arc<FileSink>> = None;

  3426	                            eprintln!(
  3427	                                "  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors"
  3428	                            );

  3463	                        sinks.push(Box::new(Arc::clone(&otlp_arc)));
  3464	                        otlp_shutdown = Some(OtlpShutdown::Sink(otlp_arc));

  3930	    /// Flush and shut down the background writer.
  3931	    ///
  3932	    /// Drops the shared sender (closing the channel) so the writer thread
  3933	    /// processes all buffered events and flushes its `BufWriter` before
  3934	    /// exiting. Joins the thread to guarantee completion.
  3935	    ///
  3936	    /// Call this at every terminal path in the worker before the tokio
  3937	    /// Runtime is dropped, or the BufWriter flush will be cancelled.
  3938	    pub async fn shutdown(&self) {
  3939	        // Drop the sender to signal EOF to the writer thread.
  3940	        *self.sender.lock().unwrap() = None;
  3941	        // Join the writer thread so the flush completes before we return.
  3942	        let handle = self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap().take();

  3944	            let _ = h.join();
  3945	        }
  3946	    }

  2860	pub fn generate_session_id() -> String {
  2861	    // Try /dev/urandom (Linux/macOS)
  2862	    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open("/dev/urandom") {
  2863	        use std::io::Read;
  2864	        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];
  2865	        if f.read_exact(&mut buf).is_ok() {
  2866	            return format!("{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}", buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]);
  2867	        }
  2868	    }
  2869	    // Fallback: PID XOR nanosecond timestamp
  2870	    let pid = std::process::id();
  2871	    let ts = Utc::now().timestamp_millis() as u64;
  2872	    let hash = pid as u64 ^ ts;
  2873	    format!("{:08x}", hash & 0xffff_ffff)
  2874	}

  6500	                Ok(())

/// Resolve configured OTLP headers without writing secrets into NEEDLE's YAML.
/// A value beginning with `env:` names an environment variable read when the
/// exporter is initialized, for example `Authorization: env:OTLP_AUTH`.
fn resolve_headers(headers: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>> {
    headers
        .iter()
        .map(|header| {
            let (key, raw_value) = header
                .split_once(':')
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid OTLP header; expected 'name: value'"))?;
            let key = key.trim();
            let raw_value = raw_value.trim();
            if key.is_empty() || raw_value.is_empty() {
                anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP header; name and value must be non-empty");
            }

            let value = if let Some(variable) = raw_value.strip_prefix("env:") {
                if variable.is_empty() {
                    anyhow::bail!("invalid OTLP header environment reference");
                }
                std::env::var(variable).map_err(|_| {
                    anyhow::anyhow!("OTLP header environment variable '{variable}' is not set")
                })?
            } else {
                raw_value.to_string()
            };
            Ok((key.to_string(), value))
        })
        .collect()
}

    Path::new(workspace)
        .file_name()

+    /// Replace the sinks owned by the background writer.
+    ///
+    /// The replacement is sent through the same FIFO channel as events. This
+    /// means every event already queued is delivered to the current sinks
+    /// before the writer installs the replacement, and events emitted after
+    /// this method returns use only the new sinks. The writer remains alive
+    /// throughout the swap.
+    ///
+    /// The writer must have been started before calling this method. Use
+    /// [`start`](Self::start) or [`start_and_wait`](Self::start_and_wait)
+    /// during initialization first.
+    pub async fn replace_sinks(&self, sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>) -> Result<()> {
+        let (reply, replaced) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
+        {
+            let sender = self
+                .sender
+                .lock()
+                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("telemetry sender lock poisoned"))?;
+            let sender = sender
+                .as_ref()
+                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("telemetry writer is shut down"))?;
+            sender
+                .send(WriterMessage::ReplaceSinks { sinks, reply })
+                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("telemetry writer channel is disconnected"))?;
+        }
+
+        replaced
+            .await
+            .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("telemetry writer stopped before replacing sinks"))
+    }

codex
The rebuild seam is transactional already: every gRPC/HTTP provider builder resolves headers before returning a candidate, and callers can replace the writer/reload layer only after `Ok`; a missing `env:` value therefore leaves the old candidate untouched. I’m tightening that contract now by making missing-variable errors fully value-free and adding regression coverage that proves each build re-reads the environment and that a failed candidate does not alter the prior resolved headers.

The targeted Cargo test is currently waiting on the shared build lock.
